KAZA UniVisa: USD 50, also covers Zimbabwe and Botswana day trips. Germany is on its eligible list, but it isn't needed just to enter Zambia.
Yellow fever: certificate needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

Visa: India is not on Zambia's visa-exemption list, so an e-visa is required.
Under 16: travellers under 16 cannot apply for their own e-visa and must be included on an accompanying adult's application.
Yellow fever: certificate needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

Air arrivals need a return ticket; land and water arrivals need sufficient funds for the stay and departure. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

fields.stay: Up to 3 months per visit

fields.cost: Free (eVisitor)
fields.note: eVisitor (subclass 651): free, multiple entry, valid 12 months from grant, up to 3 months per entry.

Separate from US immigration — an ESTA or US visa will NOT get you in. Australia is on American Samoa's list of visa waiver countries: apply online for the 30-Day Visitor Permit within 3 business days before travel.

Separate from US immigration — an ESTA or US visa will NOT get you in. The United Kingdom is on American Samoa's list of visa waiver countries: apply online for the 30-Day Visitor Permit within 3 business days before travel.

fields.stay: No stay limit stated by Gibraltar
fields.note: Gibraltar is outside the EU and Schengen, so EU free movement does not apply. German citizens are visa-exempt and may enter with a passport or a national identity card; Gibraltar's border page gives no stay limit for them.

fields.stay: No stay limit stated by Gibraltar
fields.note: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory outside the EU and Schengen, so EU free movement does not apply. Dutch citizens are visa-exempt and may enter with a passport or a national identity card; Gibraltar's border page gives no stay limit for them.

fields.stay: No stay limit stated by Gibraltar
fields.note: British Overseas Territory outside the EU and Schengen; EU free movement does not apply. Irish citizens are visa-exempt and may enter with a passport or a national identity card; Gibraltar's border page gives no stay limit for them.

fields.stay: Up to 3 months per entry; valid for 12 months or until your passport expires, whichever is shorter

fields.note: Tokelau is a self-governing territory of New Zealand. Canadians don't need a visa to enter Tokelau, but they require a permit, granted by the Council for the Ongoing Government. There is no airport: access is by boat from Apia, Samoa, usually around 24–32 hours depending on the atoll.

Genuinely hard to reach. No airport — the only access is the MV Mataliki from Apia, Samoa (roughly 24–30 hours, sailing about fortnightly). Non-residents need a permit in advance, granted by the Council for the Ongoing Government, and you must also meet Samoa's entry rules in transit.

Genuinely hard to reach. No airport — the only access is the MV Mataliki from Apia, Samoa (roughly 24–30 hours, sailing about fortnightly). Non-residents need a permit in advance, granted by the Council for the Ongoing Government, and you must also meet Samoa's entry rules in transit.

Genuinely hard to reach. No airport — the only access is the MV Mataliki from Apia, Samoa (roughly 24–30 hours, sailing about fortnightly). Non-residents need a permit in advance, granted by the Council for the Ongoing Government, and you must also meet Samoa's entry rules in transit.

Good to know: outside the US immigration zone. ESTA and US visa policy do not govern entry here.
Permit: Canada is on American Samoa's own waiver list. Apply online for the 30-Day Visitor Permit before you travel and show the emailed permit on arrival, or you can be sent back on the vessel you arrived on.
Bring: a passport valid 6 months beyond departure, a return ticket within 30 days and confirmed accommodation.

Visa: Canada is in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806. Austria's own table records a national 3-month exemption on top.
EES: the EU Entry/Exit System has been live since 10 April 2026. Expect biometric registration at the border. There is nothing to apply for.
ETIAS: not in force, and no start date has been published.
Bilateral waiver: Austria has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 1 July 1956, for 3 months (all passports). No official guidance on how to use it could be found. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: Canada is named as no-visa-required on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa schedule.
Entry form: all travellers must complete the online Immigration and Customs Form, available from 72 hours before arrival. Present the receipt on arrival.
Bring: a return ticket to your country of residence, your intended address and evidence of personal support.

Visa: Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 lists Canada among the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
EES: the EU Entry/Exit System has been live since 10 April 2026. Biometric registration at the border, nothing to apply for.
ETIAS: not in force, and no start date has been published. The Commission's own page says it is not in operation and that the EU will announce the date several months ahead.
Fee: the ETIAS fee will be EUR 20.
Bilateral waiver: Belgium has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 1 December 1949, for 2 months (all passports). Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: Canada is not on the Prohibition of Entry Order's visa-controlled list. On the contrary, a Canadian multi re-entry visa is one of the documents that lets a listed national in.
Passport: travellers who require a Multi Re-Entry Visa (MRV) must hold an MRV and a passport both valid for at least 45 days beyond the end of the visit or work permit (Government of Bermuda). Visa-exempt Canadian visitors only need a passport valid for the duration of their stay.
Good to know: the COVID-era Bermuda Travel Authorisation was abolished on 14 November 2022.

Fee: the visa fee is trivial next to the Sustainable Development Fee, which is the real cost, at USD 100 per adult per night. Ten nights for two adults is USD 2,000 in SDF against USD 80 in visa fees.
Rate: the statutory rate is USD 200 a night. The halved rate is an incentive running to 31 August 2027.
Insurance: travel insurance stopped being mandatory on 23 April 2024.

Visa: Canada is named in the 'Visa Not Required' column of the Customs & Border Control country table.
Bring: a passport valid beyond your return date, a paid return ticket and proof of funds.
Good to know: ignore the 30-day cap mentioned on that page. It applies to separately exempted categories such as people holding a US, UK or Canadian visa, not to Canadian citizens.

Visa: since 11 May 2026 all visa applications are online only. Since 21 May 2026 any visa issued outside the platform is invalid for entry. Manual entry authorisations have been abolished. Canada is not on Chad's visa-exemption list.
Apply: at least 7 days before entry and no more than 90 days ahead.
Passport: valid 6 months.
Bring: a return or onward ticket.
Registration: you must register with the national police within 72 hours of arrival.
Yellow fever: carry vaccination proof. The portal tells all applicants to have it checked on arrival.

Visa: no visa and no reciprocity fee. Chile's own visa-and-fee table lists Canada at US$0.
Stay: a Permanencia Transitoria permit of up to 90 continuous days is granted at the border.
Declaration: everyone must complete the free SAG sworn declaration for food, plant and animal products. Declare everything, the fines are real.

Visa: Canada was added to China's trial visa-free scheme from 00:00 on 17 February 2026, for business, tourism, visiting family or friends, and transit.
Expiry: the policy expires at 24:00 on 31 December 2026 (Beijing time). After that it lapses unless extended, so check before booking anything for 2027.
Not covered: the waiver does not cover work, study or news coverage. Those still need a visa in advance.
Stay: staying beyond 30 days also needs a visa obtained before you travel.

Good to know: an Australian external territory inside Australia's migration zone, so Australian visa rules simply apply.
Visa: arriving from outside Australia you need the same subclass 601 ETA as for the mainland. Canada is a listed eligible passport.
Domestic flight: arriving on a domestic flight from the Australian mainland needs no passport or visa, but photo ID must be produced for every passenger including children.

Good to know: an Australian external territory inside Australia's migration zone, so Australian visa rules apply.
Visa: the subclass 601 ETA, same as the mainland.
Domestic flight: arriving on a domestic flight from the Australian mainland needs no passport or visa, but photo ID is required for every passenger for Customs and Immigration clearance.

Visa: a tourist visa is required but is obtainable on arrival at Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport in Moroni and at other points of entry. The fee is payable in euros.
Bring: euros. Confirm current pricing with your airline.
Good to know: overstaying draws fines and possible arrest.
Yellow fever: proof is not required.

Visa: Canada is in Costa Rica's first visa group. Entry without a visa.
Stay: the length of the grant is genuinely unresolved. Costa Rica's own embassy in Canada says 180 calendar days non-extendable, while the 2022 directive in the government legal database says 90 calendar days non-extendable. The current November 2025 directive is a PDF that cannot be read. Either way, the days granted are set by the immigration officer.
Bring: an onward ticket and funds of USD 100 per month of stay. Costa Rica publishes and enforces this.

Visa check: Croatia's MFA checker returns 'No' for a Canadian ordinary passport.
Passport: Croatia attaches its own condition. The passport must be valid at least three months after your planned departure from Croatia.
Registration: short-stay registration runs through the eVisitor system and is normally handled by your accommodation provider.

Visa: Canadians are not visa-free for Cuba. A tourist visa is required before boarding, and it is now issued electronically through the Cuban Foreign Ministry's own portal. Single entry.
Stay: Canadians get a better deal than most nationalities, with 90 days rather than 30, extendable by 90 rather than 30.
Insurance: travel medical insurance with cover valid in Cuba is mandatory and must be bought before you leave. Arrive without it and you are made to buy Cuban insurance at the airport.
Form: the D'Viajeros traveller information form is mandatory. Every person including children completes it online within 48 hours before check-in.
Minors: need their own visa even if they appear in a parent's passport.

Visa: Canada is named on the Czech MFA's own exemption list. The exemption covers short-term non-profit stays only.
Registration: Czechia adds a national duty. Anyone older than 15 must register with the Foreign Police within 3 working days of arrival. Hotels register their guests, so a hotel stay covers this.
Bring: sufficient funds and medical insurance for the stay.

Visa: Dominica exempts Commonwealth citizens as a category for stays not exceeding six months. Unlike Trinidad and Tobago, it names no excluded Commonwealth states.
Canada: covered by the category rather than named individually.
Other exemption: a separate 21-day exemption exists for any bona fide tourist holding a return ticket.

Visa: Canada is named on the Dominican Republic's own category C list. Entry is on a tourist card only, no visa.
Fee: the USD 10 tourist card has been included in the price of every air ticket issued outside the Dominican Republic since 25 April 2018, so most Canadians pay nothing extra. Tickets bought inside the country do not include it.
Entry form: the free E-Ticket form is mandatory for every passenger entering or leaving, Dominican or foreign.

Visa: Canada is named on Egypt's own e-visa eligible-nationality list. Apply online at least 7 days before departure.
Visa on arrival: a 30-day visa on arrival is also available, payable in cash in US dollars only.
Sinai exception: entering by land at Taba and staying inside the Sinai Peninsula (which includes Sharm el-Sheikh) gives a 14-day visa-free stamp. To travel beyond the Sinai you need the e-visa or a 30-day visa on arrival.
Good to know: keep your entry stamp. Without it you cannot get an exit stamp.

Visa: category A, exempt from visa, on El Salvador's own foreign-ministry table.
Stay: El Salvador is part of the CA-4 zone with Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. The 90 days is a shared regional allowance set by the officer at your first CA-4 entry point, not 90 days per country.
Entry fee: neither the Salvadoran foreign ministry nor the Government of Canada publishes any entry fee for Canadians.

Visa: the Faroes are outside Schengen and a Schengen visa does not cover them. A Canadian needs nothing extra, because anyone who may enter Denmark visa-free may enter the Faroes visa-free.
Stay: the Danish Immigration Service states in terms that visa-free days in Schengen, Greenland and the Faroes share one 90-in-180 allowance.
Passport: bring a passport. An EU ID card is not enough for the territories.

Visa: Finland's MFA records Canada as having visa exemption to the Schengen area and to Finland.
Passport: Finland is strict on documents. The passport must have been issued within the last ten years and be valid at least 90 days after you intend to leave the Schengen area.
Refugee travel document: a Geneva Convention refugee travel document issued by Canada does not carry the exemption.

Passport: France requires a passport issued less than 10 years ago and valid at least 3 months beyond your departure.
Bring: proof of accommodation, funds and a return ticket.
Bilateral waiver: France has notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada (in force since 1 May 1950, 90 days, ordinary passports) that in principle allows further time in France after the Schengen 90 days. No official French guidance on how to use it could be found, so do not rely on it at the border without checking with a French consulate first.

Visa: Canadians may enter and stay visa-free for one full year. Canada is entry 40 on the list annexed to Government Ordinance No. 255 of 5 June 2015.
Stay: this is a genuine 365-day permission granted by the ordinance itself, not a 90-day stamp. It is one of the most generous allowances any country gives a Canadian passport.

Bilateral waiver: Germany's own mission in Canada publishes a usable bilateral. After your Schengen 90 days you must leave the Schengen states entirely. Then you may return to Germany, and only Germany, for a further 90 days under the German-Canadian Agreement of 17 April 1953 (in force since 1 May 1953, all passports, notified to the EU).
Good to know: keep your border exit stamps as proof.
Passport: must be valid 3 months beyond the stay and issued within the last ten years.
Work: no work on a visa-free stay.

Stay: since 15 July 2026 Gibraltar's short-stay entry conditions align with Schengen, so days in Gibraltar count against your Schengen 90/180. This is a real trap if you are combining Spain and Gibraltar.
Arriving by air: you face two sets of checks, Gibraltar immigration, then Schengen entry checks by Spanish officers, including EES biometric registration. Once through, the land border into Spain has no routine immigration checks.
UK ETA: not valid for Gibraltar.

Visa: the Greek MFA's country table lists Canada as visa-free for ordinary, diplomatic and service passports.
Bilateral waiver: Greece has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada (in force since 1 September 1959, 90 days, ordinary passports). No official Greek guidance on how it works could be found. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark but outside the EU and outside Schengen. A Schengen or Danish visa does not cover it. Canadians need nothing extra, because anyone who can enter Denmark visa-free can enter Greenland visa-free.
Stay: days in Greenland are not a separate allowance. The Danish Immigration Service states that visa-free days in Schengen, Greenland and the Faroes share one combined 90-in-180 total, so a Greenland trip does not pause or reset a Schengen clock.

Visa: Canada is named on Grenada's official visa-requirements schedule under 'No Visa Required'.
Stay: Grenada does not publish a stay period per country. Its schedule says visitors are admitted for one of 14 days, 30 days, 60 days, 90 days or 6 months, without saying which applies to whom. Do not assume 90 days.
Cruise: passengers ashore for under 24 hours need no visa regardless of nationality.

Visa: Guam is inside the United States immigration zone, so ordinary US rules apply to a Canadian. That means no visa, no ESTA and a valid passport.
Waiver program: the Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program is the wrong instrument here. Canada is not on its eligible-country list and a Canadian does not need it.
Registration: the 30-day US alien registration requirement applies on Guam exactly as on the mainland.

Stay: CA-4 zone. The 90 days is shared with El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua.
Entry form: an electronic traveller declaration must be completed before arriving and again before leaving.
Good to know: Guatemala's own government sites could not be reached, so this rests on the Government of Canada plus El Salvador's CA-4 harmonised table, which records no divergent treatment for Canada.

Visa: Canada is listed on Guyana's official schedule of countries whose nationals do not require a visa, with no duration condition attached. Several other countries on the same list carry explicit 90-day, 30-day or 14-day qualifiers, and Canada carries none.
Stay: Guyana publishes no standard visa-free stay. The endorsed period is decided by the immigration officer at the port of entry. Canada's own travel advice says a tourist visa is not required for stays up to 90 days, but the period that counts is the one stamped in your passport at entry.

Visa: no visa for Canadians for stays under 90 days. Formalities are completed on arrival.
Fee: a USD 10 tourist fee is payable at the airport by all foreign passport holders. It is a fee collected on arrival, not a visa, and cannot be bought in advance.
Visa needed: only nationals of the Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam and Yemen need a visa in advance.
Good to know: check the advisory before travelling. The security situation matters more here than the visa rule.

Rules: Vatican City publishes no immigration rules of its own and issues, checks or stamps nothing for ordinary visitors.
Borders: Vatican City is not in Schengen and not in the EU, but it has no border control with Italy. The boundary is a wall and a marble line across St Peter's Square.
In practice: your entry is governed entirely by Italy. Satisfy Schengen entry rules and you can walk in.
Good to know: museum tickets are a museum matter, not an immigration one.

Extra days: Hungary's bilateral visa waiver with Canada (notified to the EU, in force since 1 February 1991, 90 days, ordinary passports) has the clearest published rules in Europe, and its conditions are strict.
Conditions: you must not have already used up your Schengen 90 days when you enter Hungary. During the extra period you may not travel to any other Schengen state, even in transit. You must leave the Schengen area directly from Hungary on the last day.
EES: border officers record the extra days into the EES manually, so the entitlement depends on the officer doing it.
Reporting: a stay in Hungary of more than 30 days must be reported through the Enter Hungary platform.

Visa: Canada is named on India's e-Visa eligible list. The product a tourist buys is the e-Tourist Visa.
Fee: the 30-day version is seasonally priced, cheaper April to June than July to March. A 3% bank charge is added to all e-Visa fees.
Terms: the 30-day e-Tourist Visa is multiple entry, non-extendable and non-convertible.
Arrival card: an e-Arrival Card must be submitted within the 72 hours before arrival.
Scam warning: apply only at indianvisaonline.gov.in, the official website. Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of India and may charge an additional fee.

Visa: Canadians are not visa-exempt for Indonesia. You use the visa on arrival, which can be bought online in advance as an e-VOA or at the counter at an approved entry point. It cannot be converted to another stay permit.
Good to know: don't confuse it with Indonesia's 60-day B1 tourist e-visa at IDR 1,500,000, which is a different product.
Customs: an electronic customs declaration is also required of all international arrivals.

Visa: required, applied for in advance through Iran's foreign ministry e-visa portal.
Consular help: there is no Government of Canada office in Iran, so no consular help is available.
Dual citizens: dual Canadian-Iranian citizens may be required to travel on an Iranian passport and may be prevented from leaving.
Entry refusal: entry has been refused where a passport shows an Israeli visa or stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a border office adjoining Israel.

Good to know: there are two separate regimes, federal Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.
Federal Iraq: e-visa from the Ministry of Interior at evisa.iq, 30 days, single or multiple entry, used within 3 months of grant. Register with the Iraqi Residence Office after 10 days and apply for a residence permit after 3 months.
Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah): runs its own e-visa at visit.gov.krd. Canada is on its List A, 30 days, valid 90 days from issue, extendable twice to 90 days total, roughly 100,000 IQD.
Warning: a Kurdistan visa does not let you travel into the rest of Iraq.
Israeli stamps: extra screening applies if your passport shows an Israeli visa or stamp, except for Kurdistan travel.

Schengen: Ireland is not in Schengen and does not apply Schengen rules. A Schengen visa is not valid here and Irish days are entirely separate.
Visa: Canada is on Ireland's official non-visa-required list.
Authorisation: there is no pre-travel authorisation. An immigration officer stamps your passport for up to 90 days.
EES: Ireland is not participating in the EU Entry/Exit System.
Arriving from the UK: this does not exempt you from Irish immigration control.

ETA: the Isle of Man is in the Common Travel Area, not the UK, and it runs its own ETA under its own law. Applications opened 9 April 2026 and it became mandatory on 23 April 2026 for arrivals direct from outside the CTA or Ireland.
One ETA: ETAs issued by the Isle of Man, the UK, Jersey and Guernsey are mutually recognised, so one ETA covers all four.
Validity: 2 years or until your passport expires.

ETA-IL: mandatory for visa-exempt nationalities, Canada included, since 1 January 2025. Apply at least 72 hours before arrival.
Validity: up to 2 years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first. A new one is needed if you change passport, name, gender or citizenship.
Passport: must be valid at least 3 months from arrival.
Good to know: an ETA-IL only gets you to the border. The officer there decides admission.

Visa: Canada is on the Italian MFA's visa-exempt list.
Declaration: Italy adds an obligation most travellers miss, and its logic is inverted from what you would expect. If you fly into Italy directly from outside Schengen, your entry stamp discharges it. If you arrive from another Schengen country, you must file a 'dichiarazione di presenza' at the provincial Questura within 8 days, unless you are in a hotel, where the form you sign at check-in counts.
Penalty: the published consequence of not doing it is an administrative expulsion order.
Extra days: Italy has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 9 November 1952, for 3 months (all passports). No official guidance on how to use it could be found. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: exemption for short stays: tourism, business, visiting friends or relatives, with no paid activity.
Authorisation: no pre-travel authorisation is required. Visit Japan Web is a convenience service for immigration and customs, not a legal entry requirement.
Good to know: Japan's only electronic visa system is for travellers who actually need a visa. There is no 'JESTA' in force.

Allenby Bridge: no visa on arrival at the King Hussein / Allenby Bridge crossing from the West Bank. You must already hold a visa to cross there.
Visa on arrival: works at the international airports, the Sheikh Hussein Bridge and Wadi Araba (Aqaba).
Jordan Pass: bought before you arrive, it waives the 40 JOD visa fee if you stay at least 2 nights, and includes Petra.

Visa: Canada is named on Kiribati's visa-exemption list.
Stay: the 90 days is an annual allowance, not per entry.
Source: the evidence is a Kiribati government tourism page rather than the immigration ministry itself, because the ministry publishes its exemption order only as a scanned image. Confirm before a long trip.

Visa: Kuwait's own foreign ministry lists Canada among the nationalities that may either take the visa on arrival or apply through the eVisa portal. The eVisa portal is live.
Passport: valid 6+ months. The eVisa route wants a return ticket and proof of accommodation.
Entry refusal: entry is refused if the passport holds Israeli visas or stamps, or Egyptian or Jordanian stamps from an office bordering Israel.
Stay and fee: not published anywhere Hop could read without creating an account. Confirm with your airline.

Visa: Canada is named at item 10 of the statutory visa-free list under the Law on visa-free regime, covering any category of passport.
Registration: Kyrgyzstan requires foreigners to register at their place of stay within 5 working days of entry unless their nationality is on a published exemption annex. That annex is not published anywhere reachable, so Canada's position on it is not confirmed.
Good to know: hotels normally handle registration. Confirm locally if you are staying in a private home.

Visa: Canada is named on Latvia's own visa-exempt list.
Travel declaration: Latvia operates an Electronic Travel Declaration normally due 48 hours before arrival, and Canada is expressly exempt from it.
Extra days: Latvia's list of bilateral visa waiver partners does not include Canada, so there are no extra days here.

Visa: Lesotho exempts Commonwealth nationals and countries with visa-abolition agreements, and Canada is Commonwealth.
Passport: valid 6 months.
If you do need a visa: Lesotho's online e-visa system is officially suspended and applicants are directed to email the immigration department. Visa on arrival is described by Lesotho's foreign ministry as highly discouraged.
Source: no Lesotho government page names Canada specifically, so this rests on the Commonwealth exemption plus the Government of Canada.

Visa: must be obtained in advance. There is no visa on arrival.
Where to apply: visas are only issued to residents of the country where the application is made, so Canadians apply in person at the Embassy of Libya in Ottawa. Mail-in applications are not accepted.
Passport: valid at least 6 months.
Processing: normally about 20 working days.
Consular help: there is no Government of Canada office in Libya. Consular support runs from the Embassy of Canada in Tunis.

Schengen: Liechtenstein is in Schengen through its customs and visa union with Switzerland but is not in the EU.
Visa: its own Ordinance on Entry and the Granting of Visas adopts the Schengen framework wholesale. The visa requirement attaches only to Annex I nationals, and Canada is in Annex II.
Good to know: Swiss missions handle visa matters for Liechtenstein, which a visa-free Canadian never needs.

Visa: Canada is named on Malaysia's list of countries that need no visa for any purpose of entry. The Government of Canada says a tourist visa is not required for stays of up to 90 days.
Arrival card: you must complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card, an online pre-arrival form that can be filled in up to three days before arrival.
Good to know: the Government of Canada advises that the MDAC is free and to use only the official website.

Visa: a free 30-day visa is issued on arrival to every nationality except Israeli passport holders. No pre-approval.
Traveller Declaration: the form is now mandatory, not merely recommended as it once was. It must be submitted within the 96 hours before travelling in each direction.
Bring: a machine-readable passport valid at least 1 month, a confirmed onward ticket, and either a prepaid booking at a registered facility or proof of funds of USD 100 plus USD 50 per day.
Work: employment is prohibited.

Visa: Canada is named on the RMI visa-on-arrival list with the fee waived.
Conditions: a passport valid 6 months beyond your departure from the RMI, a confirmed return or onward ticket, and any visas needed for onward travel.
Not allowed: extensions, changes of status, employment, study and research are not permitted on this entry.
Fee: a USD 20 departure fee is charged, with children under 12 and adults over 60 exempt.

Visa: no visa for Canadians. Mauritius states plainly that visas and extensions of stay are issued free of charge.
Stay: the total tourist stay is capped at six months in a calendar year, granted case by case.
Bring: a valid return ticket, adequate funds and a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation.
Travel form: the online Mauritius All-in-One Travel Digital Form is a legal requirement, not optional. Refusal or false information can mean a fine of up to MUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years.
Yellow fever: proof is not required.
Overstay: overstaying is a criminal offence prosecuted in court.

Visa: the Federated States of Micronesia require no entry permit from any visitor staying 30 days or less, so a Canadian needs nothing in advance. The exemption is structural rather than a named list.
Longer stay: beyond 30 days a permit is required, and for Canadians it cannot exceed 90 days total.
Passport: must be valid at least 120 days (4 months) beyond your date of entry. That is shorter than the usual 6-month rule but is stated specifically.

Visa: Montenegro's own government names Canada explicitly.
Registration: your residence must be registered within 24 hours of arrival, and this is enforced. A hotel or other paid accommodation does it for you within 12 hours. Staying privately, you must file it yourself.
Moving: you must re-register if you move somewhere else in Montenegro for more than 24 hours.

Visa: Canada appears on Morocco's own consular exemption list with no qualifier. Several other countries on that list carry a 30-day or 90-day cap, or an AEVM pre-authorisation requirement, and Canada carries none of them.
Passport: valid at least 6 months.
Extension: to stay beyond 90 days, contact the Service aux étrangers at the local police station at least 15 days before the limit expires.
Overstay: overstaying means being held until seen by a prosecutor, and a fine.

Visa: Canada lost visa-free entry on 1 April 2025. Canadians now appear on Namibia's visa-on-arrival list and must pay.
Apply: online in advance as an e-visa, or take it on arrival at a designated port of entry. You are granted the number of days you request, to a maximum of 90 in a calendar year.
Passport: valid 6 months with 3 blank pages.
Good to know: this is confirmed from three separate Namibian government sources. Do not carry a visa-free rule forward.

Visa: a visitor visa must be obtained before travel. The application is lodged with the immigration office through a representative in person or online, not at the border.
Documents: the supporting documents are unusually heavy: certified passport pages, a 45x35mm photograph, a police certificate covering the previous 12 months, and a medical fitness certificate including a chest x-ray and blood tests.
Fee: ignore the AUD 8,000 figure that circulates. That is the media visa, on the same fee table.

Visa: the Dutch MFA's own Canada page says plainly that Canadian passport holders need no visa.
Caribbean: this covers the European part of the Kingdom only. Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten and the Caribbean Netherlands run a separate Caribbean visa regime, and a Schengen visa does not substitute for it.
Extra days: the Netherlands has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 1 January 1950, for 90 days (all passports). No rules for using it are published. Do not rely on it at the border.

Visa: Canada is on New Zealand's visa waiver list, so no visitor visa is needed in advance. A Visa Waiver Visitor Visa is then granted free on arrival.
NZeTA: you must request an NZeTA before travelling. Allow 72 hours for it. It lasts 2 years.
Fee: the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy is paid at the same time. The levy is the bigger number of the two.
Passport: must be valid at least 3 months beyond the date you plan to leave.

Visa: Nicaragua changed its visa categories in Disposición No. 002-2026, in force 16 February 2026. Canada is confirmed on the Libre Visado (visa-exempt) list at number 18.
Fee: a USD 10 tourist card is payable on arrival under the General Tourism Law. This is not mentioned in Canadian travel advice, so carry small US dollars.
Passport: must have more than six months' validity.
Stay: the officer sets the days.

Entry rules: confirmed by travel.gc.ca (25 Aug 2026). The Government of Niue and its finance ministry publish arrival and departure forms and contact details but no entry requirements, no length of stay and no visa-waiver schedule.
Law: the schedule sits in the Entry, Residence and Departure Act 1985, which is not published on any Niue government domain.
Good to know: New Zealanders enter Niue under a statutory right and are deliberately omitted from the waiver schedule, so deriving Niue's rule from New Zealand's position gives the opposite of the truth.
Contact: immigration@gov.nu before travelling.

Visa: Norfolk Island no longer runs its own immigration system. The administering department states plainly that its visa requirements are the same as Australia's.
Arriving directly: you need the subclass 601 ETA.
From the mainland: arriving from the Australian mainland needs no passport or visa, but photo ID is required.

Visa: both UDI and Norway's mission in Canada confirm Canadians need no visa.
Conditions: Norway publishes hard conditions: at least NOK 500 for each day of your stay, a passport valid at least three months beyond your planned departure, the means to travel home, and no work of any kind including remote work.
Stay: the 90 days may be split across several visits.
Extra days: Norway has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 1 January 1950, for 90 days (all passports). No rules for using it are published. Do not rely on it at the border.

Visa: Canadians apply online through Pakistan's official visa portal before travelling. Pakistan's own Consulate General in Montreal directs Canadian passport holders there.
Stay: the USD tiers are visa validity, not permitted stay per entry. Pakistan does not publish the stay on any page that could be read.
Fee: applications lodged through the consulate rather than online attract an extra CAD 50 surcharge, or CAD 60 urgent.
Processing: for Canadian passport holders it is 7–10 working days.

Visa: Canada is not on Palau's short visa-exempt list, so you take the tourist visa issued on arrival: 30 days, extendable twice by 30 days.
Fee: the cost that matters is the USD 100 Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee. The airline collects it inside your inbound fare rather than at the border, so it is easy to miss when comparing tickets.
Entry form: submit the Palau Entry Form QR code at palautravel.pw no more than 72 hours before departure.
Palau Pledge: you sign the Palau Pledge stamped into your passport on arrival.
Bring: passport valid 6 months, return ticket and sufficient funds.

Visa: there is no separate Palestinian tourist visa. The West Bank is reached through Israeli-controlled crossings using the ETA-IL and the entry card Israel issues on arrival. Keep that card, you need it to enter the West Bank.
Entry: Israeli authorities may refuse entry.
Gaza: effectively closed. Erez is shut and Rafah is extremely limited.
Allenby Bridge: crossing from Jordan at the Allenby / King Hussein Bridge requires a visa held in advance, as Jordan issues none on arrival there.

Visa: Canada is named by name in a Panamanian migration resolution, Resolución No. 22706 of 10 September 2021. It excepts citizens of the United States and Canada from the general tourist rule.
Stay: 180 days, where most nationalities get 90.
Entry conditions: Panama publishes and enforces its entry conditions: economic solvency of at least B/.500 and a confirmed booking to leave the country.

Visa: Peru's own consular table lists Canada as tourist-exempt up to 90 days. A business visit still requires a visa.
Entry card: entry and exit are recorded on the Tarjeta Andina de Migración, now digital. Printed forms have been abolished at Jorge Chávez airport and the authorised seaports, so your passport may not be stamped.
Overstay: overstaying carries a per-day fine payable on exit.

Visa: Canadians enter visa-free for up to 30 days under Executive Order 408.
Passport: Valid at least 6 months beyond the intended stay. You also need a return or onward ticket.
Good to know: Admission is at the Bureau of Immigration's discretion.
Before you fly: eTravel registration is mandatory for all incoming travellers. It can only be filed within the 72 hours before arrival and is free on the official website.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to fill it in for you are not operated by the Government of the Philippines and may charge a fee.

Visa: A short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival, via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form, for stays of up to 14 days on the same vessel.
Stay: Longer stays (15 days-6 months) need advance Entry Clearance. Apply to admin@pitcairn.gov.pn at least 3 months ahead, with a medical exam, chest X-ray and police certificates.
Fee: NZ$150 (non-refundable) for the Long-Term Visitor Visa. No fee for short visits.
Insurance: Mandatory travel/medical insurance with at least US$500,000 medevac cover for all visitors.

Passport: Poland makes the ten-year passport rule an entry condition for visa-free stays, not just a visa-application requirement. Your passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid at least three months beyond your intended departure.
Good to know: Visa-free entry does not cover residence, work or any paid activity.

Visa: Canada is named on the Portuguese MFA's own list of nationalities exempt from holding a visa.
Stay: Portugal has notified the EU of a bilateral waiver with Canada that is shorter than the Schengen allowance. It is 60 days, in force since 15 February 1958, for ordinary passports. Do not assume it adds 90.
Good to know: No official guidance on how to use it could be found. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.
Extension: An extension of stay after visa-free entry is an AIMA procedure.

Visa: Puerto Rico is inside the United States immigration zone. The Immigration and Nationality Act's definition of 'United States' expressly includes it. There is no separate Puerto Rican visa, permit or entry form.
Passport: A Canadian needs exactly what they need for Miami: a valid passport, no visa, no ESTA.
Good to know: The 30-day US registration requirement applies here too.
Good to know: Travel between Puerto Rico and the mainland is domestic, with no immigration inspection.

Stay: Romania joined Schengen in full on 1 January 2025 and internal border control with Hungary and Bulgaria ended. Romanian days now come out of the common Schengen allowance. Romania is no longer separate headroom.
Visa: Romania's exemption for Canadians also has its own domestic basis in Law no. 1108 of 25 October 2001, but that grants no extra days.
Passport: Must be valid 3 months beyond the journey and issued within the last 10 years.

Visa: A visa is required and must be obtained before travelling.
E-visa: Canada is not on the list of states whose nationals may use the unified e-visa, so that route is closed to Canadian passport holders.
How to apply: Complete the application on the MFA Consular Department's questionnaire portal and submit it in person to a Russian mission.
Migration card: On arrival, immigration officers issue a migration card. Carry it throughout the stay, present it for migration registration at the place of sojourn, and hand it to a migration officer on exit.

Visa: Canada is not on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of countries requiring a visa on entry, so no visa is needed. But it is not plain visa-free.
Before you fly: Saint Kitts launched an eTA on 26 May 2025 that applies to visa-free travellers. You must obtain one before entry.
Good to know: The eTA is valid 90 days from issue and you must travel within that window. That is the authorisation's validity, not your permitted stay, which Saint Kitts does not publish.
Good to know: The eTA is single-use. There is no need to reapply if it expires while you are in the country.
Scam warning: The government has warned about unofficial travel-authorisation sites. Use only knatravelform.kn.

Visa: Canada is named on the Department of External Affairs schedule as not requiring a visa.
Stay: 6 weeks, not three months. That is shorter than most of the Caribbean and easy to get wrong.
Bring: A return ticket is explicitly required of all visitors.
Before you fly: Complete the online customs and immigration form at travelslu.govt.lc. It is accessible no more than 72 hours before travel. Show the emailed receipt on arrival.

Good to know: This entry is the French side only. It is French but not in Schengen, and falls under the arrêté du 18 avril 2012 with Saint-Barthélemy.
Good to know: The Dutch side, Sint Maarten, is a separate country with its own rules. Do not read one entry across to the other.
Good to know: The land border is unmarked, but no official source could be found describing how it is controlled. Plan on satisfying each side's rules independently.

Visa: Saint Pierre and Miquelon is a French overseas collectivity and not part of Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid here, and time spent here is a separate allowance. Canada is on the French exemption list for these territories.
Passport: Arriving directly from Canada for 90 days or less, official Canadian photo identification is accepted instead of a passport, though a passport is simpler.
Passport: Should be valid 3 months beyond departure, hold 2 blank pages, and be less than 10 years old.

Visa: Canada is on the eligible list for the Saudi eVisa. Apply online before you travel, or take the visa on arrival at Immigration Department visa offices.
Good to know: It covers tourism, events, family visits and Umrah, but not Hajj and not study.
Passport: Valid 6 months or more.
Good to know: Overstaying attracts heavy fines and you will not be allowed to leave until they are paid.

Visa: Visa-free since 1 May 2015 and still in force. Canada is named on Senegal's own foreign-ministry exemption list.
Stay: Senegal words it as 'less than 3 months'. The Government of Canada words it as 90 days or less.
Passport: Passport or travel document valid at least 6 months.
Yellow fever: Proof only if arriving from or transiting a risk country.

Good to know: Serbia's MFA has a dedicated Canada page. The counting rule is Serbia's own, not the EU rolling window.
Good to know: Your stay must be registered within 24 hours. Hotels do it for you. If you stay privately, your host or you must register at the local police station.
Good to know: Keep the registration slip, the 'white card', until you leave.

Visa: Visa-free under the Kingdom of the Netherlands' Caribbean visa regime. Canada is on the exemption list with no island-specific restriction, unlike some nationalities that are flagged as still needing a visa for Sint Maarten.
Stay: Sint Maarten defines a tourist as someone staying no longer than three months. No residence permit or admission application is needed. Treat 90 days as the ceiling: Sint Maarten says the maximum depends on country of origin but publishes no table.
Good to know: Employment is prohibited on a tourist stay.

Visa: Slovakia's embassy in Canada states that Canadian passport holders need no visa for up to 90 days.
Bring: Slovakia publishes a funds figure of EUR 56 per person per day, plus the means to travel home. It does not accept bank or credit cards as proof.
Good to know: Stays over 30 days outside a hotel or other accommodation facility must be registered with the local Border Police within 3 working days.

Visa: Visitor visas must be applied for in advance through the e-visa portal.
Bring: A passport valid 6 months, a return or onward air ticket and proof of funds.
Good to know: Work is prohibited on a visitor visa.
Good to know: Canada is not named on any published list that can be checked. The Immigration Division's concessional-entry list is a scanned image with no text layer. Verify before travelling.

Visa: Canada is listed at 90 days on South Africa's own exemption table, with no fee.
Good to know: The electronic travel authorisation does not apply to Canadians. As of May 2026 it covers only tourists from China, India, Mexico and Indonesia, all visa-required nationalities. Expansion is stated policy, so re-check.
Passport: Valid 30 days beyond departure, with at least 2 blank pages.
Bring: Travelling with anyone under 18 requires an unabridged birth certificate. South Africa's own advisory says this applies to visa-exempt foreign nationals too. One parent travelling alone also needs an affidavit of consent from the other.

entries.destination: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

fields.note:
Good to know: There are no banks, ATMs or retail economy on the island. The Falkland Islands pound (at par with GBP) is the local currency in name only.
Visa: Entry Control Ordinance 2022 requires a visitor permit for essentially everyone, applied for via eta.entry.gov.gs. Commercial cruise operators typically submit group bookings on passengers' behalf.
Stay: A visitor permit is valid for 40 days (gov.gs).
Fee: The £50 late fee applies if you apply 8 days or less before arrival.

Stay: Canada gets an unusually generous allowance. The K-ETA eligible-countries table lists Canada at six months, where most nationalities get 90 days.
Before you fly: The K-ETA is currently waived. The Ministry of Justice extended the temporary exemption to 31 December 2026.
Fee: Unless it is extended again, the K-ETA requirement returns on 1 January 2027 at 10,000 KRW (about USD 7-8).
Good to know: You can still apply for one voluntarily if you want the pre-approval.

Visa: Spain's embassy in Ottawa confirms Canadians need no short-stay visa for tourism or business.
Bring: Unlike most of Schengen, Spain publishes hard conditions it actually enforces. You need a return or round-trip ticket in all cases, proof of accommodation or an invitation letter, and funds of EUR 122 per person per day with a floor of EUR 1,099 (about CAD 197.40 a day, minimum CAD 1,776.60). These amounts are indexed to the Spanish minimum wage and change annually.
Stay: Spain has also notified the EU of a bilateral visa waiver with Canada, in force since 25 January 1960, for 90 days (ordinary passports).
Good to know: No official guidance on how to use it could be found. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: Canada is named among the 40 countries whose nationals get the tourist ETA free. The ETA is still required. Only the fee is waived. Apply before you arrive.
Stay: On a second entry you get only the balance of the original 30 days, not a fresh 30.
Good to know: The current arrangement is set out in Alert 01, effective 25 May 2026. Sri Lanka has changed this repeatedly, so check before you travel.
Scam warning: eta.gov.lk is the only official website. Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Sri Lanka and may charge an additional fee.

Visa: Visas are not granted automatically. Allow at least two months between applying and travelling. Sudan's own missions list entry visas for business, official, work, humanitarian and tourist purposes.
Good to know: You must register with the Aliens' Registration Office within 3 days of arrival. A separate permit is needed to travel outside Khartoum.
Good to know: The Embassy of Canada in Sudan has suspended operations. There is no Canadian consular support inside the country. Heavy fighting has continued since April 2023.
Yellow fever: Proof is not required.

Visa: Not plain visa-free, and getting this wrong would strand you at check-in. Canadians travel without a visa but must buy a paid Entry Fee voucher for every entry.
Before you fly: Since 15 January 2024 the voucher must be shown to airline staff before boarding. Buy it online before you fly.
Good to know: CARICOM nationals and holders of a Surinamese visa or residence permit are exempt from the fee. Canadians are not.

Visa: Svalbard is Norwegian but sits outside the Schengen area under the Svalbard Treaty. It is visa-free for every nationality. You need only a valid travel document.
Good to know: There is effectively no route except through mainland Norway, which is Schengen. You leave Schengen to enter Svalbard and re-enter it coming home, so your Schengen 90/180 allowance must have room for both transits. Days on Svalbard itself are not Schengen days.
Good to know: Since 1 January 2026, travel outside the 'travel area' needs an application or registration, with four weeks' lead time. The travel area is central Longyearbyen, the airport, Pyramiden, Barentsburg and Ny-Ålesund. Organised tours are covered by the operator.

Visa: Sweden's missions confirm Canadians need no visa for 90 days or less. Canada is named in Sweden's list of bilateral visa-exemption partners.
Stay: That agreement was notified to the EU, has been in force since 30 June 1949, and covers 3 months (ordinary passports). Under it the 90 days are counted across the Nordic area: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden. Only prior time in a Nordic country within the last 6 months is deducted. In principle that means Schengen time elsewhere doesn't count against it.
Good to know: It is a documented entitlement, but Migrationsverket does not publicise it and border systems work to the Schengen 90/180. Do not treat it as reliable. Confirm with a consulate before relying on it.

Visa: The Swiss State Secretariat for Migration's own per-nationality list carries a Canada row reading 'No' visa for stays up to 90 days.
Good to know: Canada's row carries footnote V1. A visa is required for gainful work in construction, catering, cleaning, security or erotic services, or for any other work over 8 days in a calendar year.
Stay: Switzerland has no bilateral agreement with Canada. A Canadian gets the Schengen 90/180 and nothing more.

Visa: Canada is named on Taiwan's visa-exempt list. Canadian and UK passport holders get an extension right most nationalities don't have.
Passport: Valid at least six months. You need a confirmed return or onward ticket.
Before you fly: The Taiwan Arrival Card has been mandatory for all inbound travellers since 1 October 2025. It is free.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Taiwan and may charge an additional fee.

Stay: Thailand's 60-day visa exemption was revoked by Cabinet on 19 May 2026 and the tourism exemption reverts to 30 days. It takes effect 15 days after Royal Gazette publication. Canada is on the 30-day exemption table.
Before you fly: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is required of all non-Thai nationals. It is free. File it within the 3 days before arrival, including the arrival date, and only at tdac.immigration.go.th.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to fill it in for you are not operated by the Government of Thailand and may charge a fee.

Visa: A visa on arrival is available to travellers of any nationality except those covered by a visa-waiver agreement. Canada is not in that waiver group.
Good to know: It is single entry, except for travellers to Oecussi, who may receive multiple entries.
On arrival: A disembarkation and embarkation card must be completed on arrival.

Visa: Canada is named on Tonga's visa-on-arrival country list. The stay is 30 days, not 31.
Bring: A passport with at least 6 months validity, a valid return ticket out of the Kingdom, and proof of sufficient funds.
Fee: Ignore the USD 69 figure that circulates. That is an embassy processing fee for visas applied for abroad, not the on-arrival cost.

Visa: Canada is named on the Ministry of Homeland Security's own list of countries whose citizens do not require a visa. Canada is also not among the eleven Commonwealth states Trinidad and Tobago carves out of its exemption by name. Both directions confirm it.
Stay: Trinidad and Tobago publishes no permitted stay for visa-exempt visitors. The landing time is stamped at the officer's discretion.

Visa: Changed. Canadians no longer need an e-visa. Türkiye exempted Canadian ordinary passport holders from the visa requirement, announced by its missions in Canada on 8 February 2024.
Good to know: The exemption covers ordinary passports and touristic travel only. Official and diplomatic passport holders still need a visa, as do other travel purposes such as work or study.

Visa: No visa is issued without a Letter of Invitation certified by the State Migration Service. A tourist not visiting anyone in particular gets the invitation from an authorized travel agency in Turkmenistan. The invitation is valid 3 months from certification.
Good to know: A visa can be stamped on arrival at Ashgabat airport, but only if you already hold the certified invitation. So this is not a visa on arrival in any ordinary sense.

Visa: Canada is named on the TCI Border Force visa-exempt list. TCI sets its own policy and the UK ETA does not apply.
Passport: Validity differs by nationality. Border Force states US, UK and Canadian citizens need a passport valid for the duration of stay, while other visitors need six months.
Stay: No permitted stay period is published by TCI itself.

Visa: A visitor's permit is granted on arrival.
Fee: Canadians pay for it. Canada is not on Tuvalu's fee-exemption schedule, though the UK, Fiji, Tonga, Nauru, Niue and dozens of others are.
Bring: A valid onward ticket.
Extension: A permit or extension is only granted if you have not spent more than 3 months in Tuvalu in the 12 months before.

Visa: Ukraine's MFA entry-regime table lists Canada as visa-free for up to 90 days per 180.
Good to know: Martial law is in force and conditions on the ground change. Check the MFA and your airline before travelling.
Stay: The State Migration Service counts the 90 days by looking back 180 days from the date of the check. It operates an in-country extension procedure.

Visa: Free visa on arrival, stamped at the port of entry. The UAE's residency directorate names Canada on its visa-on-arrival list.
Stay: The 90-day figure comes from the Government of Canada. The UAE's own portal publishes separate 30-day and 90-day categories but does not make the country lists readable. Confirm with your airline if you plan a long stay.
Passport: Valid 6 months or more. Leave on the same passport you entered on.

Visa: Canadians need no US visa and are not Visa Waiver Program travellers, so ESTA does not apply.
Good to know: Since 11 April 2025, and under a final rule effective 29 June 2026, any foreign national aged 14 or over who stays 30 days or longer must be registered and fingerprinted. DHS named Canadians specifically as the gap. Many are admitted at land borders with no I-94, so they were never registered.
Form G-325R: if you did not get an I-94 or an admission stamp, file Form G-325R with USCIS before day 30. Snowbirds driving south for the winter are squarely inside this.
Bring: Registered travellers 18 and over must carry their evidence of registration at all times. Wilful failure to register is punishable by a fine of up to USD 5,000 or six months' imprisonment.
Good to know: This is about citizenship. Canadian permanent residents who are not citizens do need a visa.

Visa: The US Virgin Islands are inside the United States immigration zone. The INA's definition of 'United States' expressly includes them. No separate USVI visa or permit exists, and the 30-day US registration requirement applies.
Good to know: The only USVI-specific immigration rule in the regulations is a waiver for British Virgin Islands nationals, which has no bearing on Canadians.
Good to know: The USVI sits outside the US customs territory, so expect a customs inspection flying back to the mainland.

Visa: Canada is on Uzbekistan's visa-free list in the 30-day category. No visa and no e-visa needed.
Good to know: You must be registered at your place of stay within three days of arrival, excluding weekends and public holidays. Hotels and licensed accommodation do this automatically and issue a registration slip. Keep every slip, because they can be checked when you leave.
Good to know: Staying in a private home means arranging the registration yourself.

Visa: Canada is not on Venezuela's tourist-visa exemption list. The list runs to 71 countries and Canada is absent. You must hold a visa before travelling. None are issued on arrival, and the penalties for arriving without one include lengthy detention.
Good to know: Canada's embassy in Caracas has been closed since 2019 and consular help is run remotely from Bogotá.
Passport: Canadian-Venezuelan dual nationals must enter and leave on a Venezuelan passport.

Visa: Canada is Category B. You do not apply in advance, but you must pay for and obtain a visa when you enter. You can also buy it online beforehand.
Passport: Valid 6 months with 2 blank pages.
Good to know: The KAZA UNIVISA is the better buy if you are doing Victoria Falls. USD 50 covers Zimbabwe and Zambia with multiple entries for up to 30 days, and permits Botswana day trips through Kazungula. Canada is eligible.

Approval: Germany's Federal Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt, UBA) says Germans planning an Antarctic activity need its approval, and names tourists among those who apply.
Before you book: use an IAATO-member tour operator, and check with the operator or the UBA whether your trip needs German approval.
Season: October-April.
Good to know: the departure country (commonly Argentina or Chile) has its own entry rules.

Insurance: since 1 January 2026, entry requires foreign health insurance for the whole stay covering at least GEL 30,000 (about EUR 10,000), printed or electronic, in English or Georgian.
Work, study or family: for these, get a residence permit at a Public Service Hall in time to be granted within the 360-day visa-free period.

Passport: valid 6+ months from arrival.
Entry stamp: make sure your passport is stamped. Some CA-4 land borders don't stamp, and a missing stamp can bring a fine of up to USD 250.
Pre-register: at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before arrival and departure, and carry the confirmation.
Stay: the CA-4 allowance is 90 days from first entry. An extension is possible, up to 120 days in total in the CA-4 area.

Entry: EEA nationals may enter with a valid travel document.
Permit: needed for any gainful activity, or for a stay without work of more than three months within six months. A non-working permit needs sufficient means and comprehensive health insurance.
Register: a permit holder must register with the municipal residents' office within eight days of arrival.

Visa: required. Normally issued by the North Korean embassy in Berlin (exceptionally another DPRK embassy, e.g. Beijing).
Invitation: always required from the Korean side. Processing takes at least four weeks.
Passport: must be valid at least three months from entry.
Extension: possible locally only in exceptional cases.

Visa on arrival: free at the airport for tourist stays up to 14 days, with a return ticket, hotel reservation and proof of sufficient funds. The 14-day stay cannot be extended.
Longer: for up to 30 days, a visa is available for a fee on entry. Longer multiple-entry visas (up to one year) are applied for before travel.
Passport: travel documents must be valid at least 6 months after entry.
Overstay: penalty of OMR 10 per day.

Visa: there is no separate Palestinian visa. Israel controls entry to the West Bank.
Before travel: get an approved ETA-IL. Israeli immigration issues an entry card at the crossing that governs access to Palestinian Authority areas.
Gaza: crossings are closed, Erez from Israel, and Rafah from Egypt since 6 May 2024.

Visa: no advance application needed for a visit of 14 days or less on the same vessel. A short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form.
Getting there: there is no airport. All travel is by the Government's vessel from Mangareva (French Polynesia), at least two nights each way.

Visa: Svalbard is part of Norway, but the Norwegian Immigration Act does not apply, so foreigners need no visa or work and residence permit to go there.
Requirements: everyone, foreign or Norwegian, must meet the 'rejection and expulsion' requirements, including having the means to reside.
Passport: a valid passport or accepted ID is required for travel.

Stay: under the EU-Swiss free movement agreement, EU/EFTA citizens can stay without a permit for three months.
After that: a permit from the cantonal authority is needed, for example a job-seeker permit or a permit for non-working persons, which needs sufficient financial means and health and accident insurance.
Register: those taking up residence without work must register with the local authorities within 14 days of arrival.

Visa: apply online before travel. Biometrics are taken at the point of entry.
Approval: lapses 90 days after approval if unused.
Yellow fever: certificate is no longer mandatory for entry (Uganda notice, 2 October 2026).
Good to know: the East Africa Tourist Visa (USD 100, multiple entry, 90 days) covers Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda.

Passport: valid 6+ months from arrival. Passport cards are not accepted.
Pre-registration: pre-register at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before arrival and departure, and carry the confirmation.
Entry stamp: get a stamp on entry. Some CA-4 land borders do not stamp, and a missing stamp can mean a fine of up to USD 250.
Stay: CA-4 allowance is 90 days from first entry. Honduras' INM can extend a tourist stay by up to 90 more days.
Good to know: some UK-born Irish citizens have been caught by the 2024 visa rule for UK tourists. Contact the Irish Embassy in Mexico.

Entry: EEA nationals may enter with a valid travel document.
Permit: needed for any gainful activity, or for a stay without work of more than three months within six months. A permit holder must register with the municipal residents' office within eight days of arrival.
Non-working permit: needs sufficient means and comprehensive health insurance.

Visa: required since 1 April 2025, available on arrival or as an e-visa.
Passport: valid at least 6 months beyond arrival, with at least 3 blank pages.
Travellers under 18: need a full unabridged birth certificate showing both parents' details, or an affidavit of consent if not travelling with both parents or legal guardians.

Visa: there is no separate Palestinian visa. Israel controls entry to the West Bank.
Before travel: get an approved ETA-IL. Israeli immigration issues an entry card at the crossing that governs access to Palestinian Authority areas.
Gaza: Erez crossing is closed, and Rafah has been closed to general traffic since 6 May 2024.

Visa: the multiple-entry, 1-year tourist eVisa allows 90 days in total, non-renewable. Apply online in preference to visa on arrival (credit card or MADA only).
Passport: valid at least 6 months from entry. Passport cards are not accepted.
Good to know: non-Muslims may not enter the Holy Mosque in Makkah or the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah.

Visa: Svalbard is part of Norway, but the Norwegian Immigration Act does not apply, so foreigners need no visa or work and residence permit to go there.
Conditions: everyone, foreign or Norwegian, must meet the 'rejection and expulsion' requirements, including having the means to reside.
Passport: a valid passport or accepted ID is required for travel.

Stay: under the EU-Swiss free movement agreement, EU/EFTA citizens can stay without a permit for three months.
After that: a permit from the cantonal authority is needed, for example a job-seeker permit or a permit for non-working persons, which needs sufficient financial means and health and accident insurance.
Registration: required with the local authorities for those taking up residence without work, within 14 days of arrival.

Visa: on arrival, or apply online in advance at evisa.gov.zw. Processing averages 7 working days, so apply at least 3 weeks ahead.
Multiple entry: not available on arrival for Irish passports. Apply online.
KAZA UniVisa: 1-month validity. It covers Zimbabwe and Zambia, plus Botswana day trips at Kazungula.

Visa: required for ordinary passports. Use the e-visa, or get a visa on arrival if you hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU/Schengen states, the USA, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, the UK, Canada, Russia or Japan, or a UAE, Saudi, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain or Oman residence permit.
Bring: without one of those, bring travel insurance, a return air ticket, an invitation letter and proof of funds.
Insurance: travel/medical insurance is mandatory for the e-visa.

Visa: required, unless you hold a valid US visa (not C transit) or US Green Card with 6+ months' validity. Then you are visa-free for up to 90 days with proof of sufficient funds.
Apply: otherwise apply via SAC Ciudadanos to the Chilean Embassy in New Delhi or Consulate General in Mumbai.
Good to know: no visa on arrival; processing can take up to 6 months.

Visa: Visa V (Visitor) required, unless you hold a valid Schengen or US residence permit, or a Schengen or US visa with at least 180 days' validity left on arrival. Then you may be allowed in without a visa.
Transit: a transit visa is needed even for direct airport transit.
Before you fly: Check-Mig online pre-registration is recommended.

Visa: required in advance; not available on arrival.
Exemption: if the passport already holds a French multiple-entry visa valid 6 months to 5 years.
Passport: valid 3+ months beyond departure, 2 blank pages, issued within the last 10 years.
Show: accommodation, funds, a return or onward ticket and trip purpose.

Visa: a Visitor's Visa is required before travel. There is no visa-free or on-arrival option. No sponsorship letter is needed.
Documents: certified passport ID-page copies, a passport photo, a police clearance covering the last 12 months' residence, and a medical fitness certificate.
Passport: must not expire within 3 months of applying.

Visa: India is not on Israel's ETA-IL list, so Indian nationals need Israel's e-Visa.
Entry: there is no separate Palestinian visa. Israeli immigration issues the entry card at the crossing that governs access to Palestinian Authority areas.
Crossings: Gaza's Erez crossing is closed, and Egypt's Rafah crossing has been closed to general traffic since 6 May 2024.

Visa: no advance application for a visit of 14 days or less on the same vessel. The immigration officer grants a short-term visitor visa on arrival via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form.
Getting there: there is no airport. Travel is by the Government vessel from Mangareva (French Polynesia), at least two nights each way.

Permit: South Korea requires its nationals to get an Antarctic activity permit from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs before any Antarctic trip, tourism included.
Penalty: going without one can mean up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million.
Before you fly: book through an IAATO-member tour operator and apply to the Ministry before you travel.
Season: October-April.
Good to know: the departure country (commonly Argentina or Chile) has its own entry rules.

Visa: visa-free. South Korea's foreign ministry lists 90 days for Barbados under an agreement.
Before you fly: complete the online Immigration and Customs Form, available from 72 hours before arrival.
Bring: a passport valid for the trip, a return ticket to your country of residence, your intended address and evidence of personal support.

Visa: visa-free for up to 30 days, by air only. You must both arrive and leave through one of Belarus's designated airports: Minsk National, Brest, Gomel, Grodno, Mogilev or Vitebsk.
Not covered: flights to or from Russia, which carry no border control, and entry overland.
Insurance: medical insurance of at least EUR 10,000, valid in Belarus, is mandatory.

Passport: valid at least 6 months from arrival.
Entry stamp: make sure you get a stamp on entry. Some CA-4 land borders don't stamp, and no stamp can mean a fine of up to USD 250.
Pre-registration: pre-register online at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before arrival and departure, and carry the confirmation.
Stay: the CA-4 allowance runs 90 days from first entry.
Extension: Honduras' INM can extend a tourist stay by up to 90 more days.

Visa: approval is normally arranged by a travel agency in Iran. Otherwise register at evisa.mfa.ir with a hotel booking, flight ticket and vaccination certificate.
Passport: valid more than 6 months.
Insurance: travel insurance is mandatory since 21 May 2024, issued with the visa.
Good to know: passports showing travel to Israel are refused.

Visa: visa-free for 90 days in any 180.
Extra stay: under a bilateral waiver, a South Korean who stays inside Latvia after the Schengen allowance can remain up to another 90 days. Then you must leave Schengen or go only to a Schengen state with its own bilateral agreement.
Re-entry: after a 90-day interval. Keep proof of time outside Latvia if stamps don't show it.

Visa: apply online before travel. Biometrics are taken at the chosen point of entry.
Yellow fever: a certificate is no longer mandatory for entry (Uganda notice, 2 October 2026).
Validity: an approved visa lapses 90 days after approval if unused.
Good to know: the East Africa Tourist Visa (USD 100, multiple entry, 90 days) covers Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda.

Visa: South Korea is on the Venezuelan foreign ministry's list of countries exempt from the tourist visa for entry by air. South Korea's foreign ministry (0404.go.kr) states that Korea and Venezuela have an agreement allowing 90 days visa-free.
Bring: immigration may ask to see a flight ticket leaving within 90 days and proof of accommodation, so carry both.

Visa: on-arrival visas ended at the end of 2012.
Permit: Korean law requires an exceptional passport use permit from Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs before a Korean passport is used to enter Yemen. Travel without it risks a fine of up to KRW 10 million or one year's imprisonment.
Good to know: the permit is separate from any Yemeni visa.

Passport: valid at least 6 months from arrival.
Pre-register: at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before arrival and departure. Carry the confirmation.
Entry stamp: make sure you get stamped. Some CA-4 land borders don't stamp, and a missing stamp can bring a fine of up to USD 250.
Stay: the CA-4 allowance (Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua) is 90 days from first entry.
Extension: Honduras' INM can extend a tourist stay by up to 90 more days.

Entry: EEA nationals may enter with a valid travel document.
Permit: needed for any gainful activity, or for a stay without work of more than three months within six months.
Register: a permit holder must register with the municipal residents' office within eight days of arrival.
Non-working permit: needs sufficient means and comprehensive health insurance.

Visa: required since 1 April 2025, available on arrival or as an e-visa.
Passport: must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival, with at least 3 blank pages.
Under 18: travellers need a full unabridged birth certificate showing both parents' details, or an affidavit of consent if not travelling with both parents or legal guardians.

Visa: apply for the eVisa online or buy a visa on arrival.
Passport: must be valid at least 6 months from departure.
Hajj and Umrah: need separate visas via Nusuk.
Overstay: overstaying the 90 days brings fines and possible exit restrictions until paid.
Good to know: non-Muslims may not enter the Holy Mosque in Makkah or the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah.

Visa: EU passports (official, diplomatic and ordinary) are covered by Solomon Islands' mutual visa arrangement with the EU. Visa fee exempted, maximum stay 90 days, single entry, work prohibited.
Apply: online through the e-visa portal from outside Solomon Islands, with a sponsor support letter, your passport biopage, a return ticket and a cover letter giving the purpose of travel.
Grant letter: emailed to you. You must present a copy when you enter.
Passport: you may not be allowed in if your passport validity is less than 6 months.

Entry Fee: Dutch citizens are not exempt. Tourism and family-visit travellers need no visa but must pay it and carry proof at check-in and on arrival.
Visa: business, work, study or transit needs a visa from the Consulate-General in Amsterdam.
Form: travellers 18+ must complete the online ICF form within 7 days of travel.

Visa: Svalbard is part of Norway, but the Norwegian Immigration Act does not apply, so foreigners need no visa or work and residence permit to go there.
Conditions: everyone, foreign or Norwegian, must meet the 'rejection and expulsion' requirements, including having the means to reside.
Passport: a valid passport or accepted ID is required for travel.

Stay: under the EU-Swiss free movement agreement, EU/EFTA citizens can stay without a permit for three months.
Permit: after that a permit from the cantonal authority is needed, for example a job-seeker permit or a permit for non-working persons. The non-working permit needs sufficient financial means and health and accident insurance.
Register: required with the local authorities for those taking up residence without work, within 14 days of arrival.

Visa: apply online before travel. Biometrics are taken at the point of entry.
Yellow fever: certificate no longer mandatory for entry (Uganda notice, 2 October 2026).
Approval: lapses 90 days after issue if unused.
Good to know: the East Africa Tourist Visa (USD 100, multiple entry, 90 days) covers Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda.

Good to know: Åland is an autonomous region of Finland and fully inside the Schengen area. Finland's rules apply.
Stay: Days spent here count toward the same 90/180 allowance as anywhere else in Schengen.
Getting there: Reached by ferry from Turku, Helsinki or Stockholm. There is no separate immigration control.
Tax: Åland sits outside the EU VAT and excise area, which is why the ferries run duty-free shops. That is a tax boundary, not an immigration one.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The EU Entry/Exit System is live.

Good to know: American Samoa runs its own immigration system. A US ESTA is not valid here.
Visa: New Zealand is on American Samoa's waiver list. NZ citizens apply online for a 30-day visitor permit at least 72 hours before travel.
Required: Passport valid 6 months beyond departure, return ticket, accommodation and a local contact.

Visa: No visa or ETA is applied for in advance. Presenting a valid NZ passport and passenger card counts as applying for the Special Category visa (subclass 444), granted at the border subject to health and character checks.
Good to know: The visa ceases on departure and is re-granted each entry. It does not itself lead to permanent residence.

ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The EU Entry/Exit System is live (fully operational 10 April 2026), so expect fingerprints and a facial image at the border instead of a passport stamp.
Bilateral agreement: Austria holds a 1.6.1958 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 3 months. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (ordinary, diplomatic and service passports). Do not rely on it without checking first.

Visa: Bahrain's own eligibility engine (evisa.gov.bh) shows two visas for a New Zealand passport on a general tourist visit, both obtainable at the Arrival Counter: Visit Visa 2 Weeks Single Entry (2-week stay) and Visit Visa Three Months Multiple Entry (1 month per entry).
Online: The same nationality also qualifies for four visas online, including One Year and 5 Year multiple-entry options allowing 90 days per visit. Applying in advance buys a longer stay than turning up does.
Country lists: Ignore Bahrain's published country lists as a guide to eligibility. They name all 204 countries and mark every one “conditions apply”.
Fee: The fees shown are Bahrain’s published eVisa fees. That fee list does not cover the Arrival Counter, so check the counter fee when you arrive.

ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The Entry/Exit System is live (fully operational 10 April 2026), so expect fingerprints and a facial image at the border instead of a stamp.
Bilateral agreement: Belgium holds a 15.11.1951 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 2 months. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (all passports). Do not rely on it without checking first.

Visa: Only India, Bangladesh and the Maldives are exempt from the advance e-visa. New Zealanders must hold an approved visa before flying.
Fee: The real cost is the compulsory Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of USD 100 per adult per night. It is separate from the visa fee and far larger.
Good to know: Reduced SDF applies to children, and a 24-hour waiver applies in four border towns.

Visa: New Zealand is not in Cambodia's exemption tables, so a tourist visa is needed. It is available on arrival at airports and major land crossings, or in advance online.
Official site: Only evisa.gov.kh is the official e-visa website.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Cambodia and may charge an additional fee.
Arrival card: All travellers must also submit the free e-Arrival card within 7 days before arrival.
Passport: Needs 6+ months validity.

Visa: Since 2026 all Chad visa applications must be lodged online. New Zealand is not on Chad's visa-exemption list.
Apply: Apply at least 7 days before arrival and no more than 90 days ahead.
Yellow fever: A certificate is required.
Stay: The 30-day figure comes from an embassy page that predates the online-only change, so confirm when applying.

Visa: New Zealand is on China's unilateral visa-free list for ordinary passports, covering tourism, business, visiting family or friends, exchange visits and transit.
