Trial policy: This is a trial policy that expires at 24:00 on 31 December 2026 and has to be re-checked before then.
Stay: Stays longer than 30 days still need a visa arranged in advance.
Transit: The separate 240-hour visa-free transit scheme is a different thing and only applies if you are passing through to a third country.

Territory: An Australian external territory inside the Australian migration zone, so Australian immigration law applies exactly as on the mainland.
Visa: Presenting a valid New Zealand passport counts as applying for the Special Category visa (subclass 444), which Home Affairs grants on arrival, free of charge, subject to health and character checks. Home Affairs says “if you apply on arrival in Australia, your application will be processed at the airport or seaport”.
Good to know: The visa ceases when you leave and is re-granted on each entry.
Getting there: Flights arrive via Perth, where you are cleared into Australia.
Biosecurity: Strict.

Territory: An Australian external territory inside the Australian migration zone, so Australian immigration law applies exactly as on the mainland.
Visa: Presenting a valid New Zealand passport counts as applying for the Special Category visa (subclass 444), granted on arrival free of charge subject to health and character checks. It ceases when you leave and is re-granted on each entry.
Getting there: Flights arrive via Perth, usually routing through Christmas Island, and you are cleared into Australia at Perth.
Good to know: Biosecurity is strict and there is no hospital on the islands.

Visa: eVisaCuba, the Cuban Foreign Ministry's official electronic visa portal, states that “the tourist visa is valid for a single entry to Cuba, for a stay of 90 days, extendable for 90 days”. This is the replacement for the old paper tourist card.
Fee: The portal does not publish a fee or an exempt-nationality list, and Cuba's foreign ministry and diplomatic sites would not load at all, so the price is unconfirmed.
Not confirmed: Two further requirements are widely applied but not stated on this portal and were not confirmed: the D'Viajeros online traveller declaration and compulsory travel medical insurance.
Timing: Allow 72 business hours for a decision.

Visa: Entry is on a Tourist Card, for tourism only. Business travel needs a consular visa.
Fee: The USD 10 card has been built into air tickets issued outside the Dominican Republic since 2018, so most travellers have already paid it.
Before you fly: The free electronic entry/exit form (E-Ticket) is compulsory for every passenger.

Visa: New Zealand is on Egypt's e-visa eligible list, which is the route officially confirmed for NZ passports. Apply at least 7 days before departure.
Passport: Must be valid 6+ months.
Do not rely on: A visa on arrival exists but no Egyptian source confirms it for New Zealanders. The often-quoted free South Sinai entry stamp for Sharm El Sheikh arrivals could not be confirmed from any Egyptian government page either. Do not rely on either.

Stay: The 90 days is a single allowance covering El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua together. Crossing between them does not reset the clock, and overstay is assessed regionally. Leaving the CA-4 area entirely starts a fresh period.
Nicaragua: As of 2026, Nicaragua now requires New Zealanders to hold a Visa Consultada under Disposición 002-2026. Even though Nicaragua is a CA-4 member, you cannot cross into it on this permit. Treat the practical free-movement zone as El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras.

Good to know: The Faroes are not in the Schengen area and a Schengen visa does not admit you, but New Zealanders need no visa either way.
Stay: Days spent here do count towards the same 90-in-180 total as Schengen. The Danish Immigration Service says so explicitly, so the common claim of a separate allowance is wrong.

ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The EU Entry/Exit System is live.
Stay: Staying beyond 90 days means applying for a residence permit from outside Finland, not extending in country.
Bilateral agreement: Finland holds a 1973 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (ordinary passports). No government guidance explains how to use it at the border, so do not rely on it without checking first.

Stay: France gives New Zealanders an extra 90 days beyond the Schengen allowance, but only in metropolitan France and only after the Schengen 90 days. Taking the bilateral days first and then travelling elsewhere in Schengen makes you an overstayer.
Border: You must identify yourself to a French border officer so your Entry/Exit System record is manually adjusted.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Bilateral agreement: France holds a 1.12.1947 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (not stated).

Change: Gibraltar's arrangements changed materially on 15 July 2026. It is not in Schengen but now aligns its short-stay visa policy with Schengen under the EU/UK treaty, and Schengen-style border checks and the Entry/Exit System apply at the airport and port.
Visa: New Zealand is named on Gibraltar's own exemption list.
ETIAS: Will apply to Gibraltar once the system is operational (UK gov.uk foreign travel advice, checked 26 Sep 2026).

Visa: Greece's own foreign ministry table lists New Zealand as visa-free on all passport types.
Entry/Exit System: Biometric registration is live.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Bilateral agreement: Greece holds a 6.12.1961 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (ordinary passports). No government guidance explains how to use it at the border, so do not rely on it without checking first.

Good to know: Guadeloupe is a French overseas department and is not in the Schengen area. A Schengen visa gives no right of entry here, and days spent here do not count against your Schengen 90/180.
Visa: New Zealand appears in the French government's exemption table for these territories with no special conditions attached.

Visa: Guam counts as the United States for Visa Waiver Program purposes, so a New Zealander flies in on an approved ESTA and is admitted for up to 90 days.
Other option: There is a separate Guam-CNMI waiver that gives only 45 days and only for Guam and the Northern Marianas. ESTA is the better route.
Fee: The ESTA fee is adjusted for inflation annually, so re-check it.

Visa: The Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración's current country classification places “Nueva Zelandia” in Categoría A, exento de visa. Entry is on a valid passport alone.
Stay: The 90 days is a single allowance covering Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua together. Moving between them does not reset it, and leaving the CA-4 region entirely voids the permit.
Nicaragua: As of 2026, Nicaragua now requires New Zealanders to hold a Visa Consultada, so you cannot simply cross into Nicaragua on this permit even though it is a CA-4 member. Treat the practical free-movement zone as Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras.

Visa: Since 23 April 2026 a New Zealander flying direct to Guernsey from outside the Common Travel Area needs a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation. Guernsey uses the UK scheme and portal.
Via the UK: Arriving via the UK, the same ETA covers you and there are no routine controls on the UK–Guernsey leg.
Good to know: All three Crown Dependencies joined on the same date, and one ETA covers the UK, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man.

Visa: New Zealand is on Guyana's visa exemption schedule, confirmed on three separate government sources.
Stay: None of them states how long a visa-exempt visitor may stay. The one-month figure that circulates comes from Guyana's visa fee schedule, which by its own wording applies only to nationalities that do need a visa.

Good to know: The Vatican publishes no entry, visa or border rule at all and operates no passport control. You arrive having already been admitted to Italy, so the Italian and Schengen rules are what actually govern.
Not immigration: Do not confuse this with the dress code and ticketing rules for St Peter's and the Museums. Those are venue conditions, not immigration.
Changes: If Italy's entry rules change, notably when ETIAS starts, this changes with them.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: Iceland also has a 1974 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand (in force 1.2.1974, all passports). Iceland says New Zealand citizens may stay up to 3 months beyond the 90 days allowed in the Schengen area.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The Entry/Exit System is live.

Apply: Apply online at least 4 days before arrival and enter only through a designated airport or seaport.
Limits: The e-Visa cannot be extended or converted, and it is not valid for Protected, Restricted or Cantonment areas.
Official site: Apply through the official website of the Government of India, indianvisaonline.gov.in.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of India and may charge an additional fee.

Visa: Iraq suspended visa on arrival for New Zealanders. Get an e-visa before you fly.
Conflicting sources: One Iraqi consulate page still advertises visa on arrival at USD 75 and has not been withdrawn, so Iraq's own sources contradict each other. The e-visa is the later instruction.
Kurdistan Region: It runs a completely separate visa system (30 days, extendable to 90, about USD 72 online). The two systems are not interchangeable.

Good to know: Ireland is not in the Schengen area. It is in the EU and in the Common Travel Area with the UK, so the Schengen 90/180 and ETIAS do not apply here.
Visa: New Zealand is named in Ireland's statutory visa order.
Before you fly: Ireland has not introduced any electronic travel authorisation of its own, so as at August 2026 there is nothing to apply for before you fly.

ETA: New since 23 April 2026. An ETA is required for New Zealanders arriving from outside the Common Travel Area.
Via other places: An ETA is required even when travelling via Ireland, Jersey or Guernsey, unless already lawfully resident/permitted in the Common Travel Area.
Exempt: British and Irish citizens, and non-visa nationals already living in Ireland or holding existing CTA immigration permission.
Coverage: Otherwise, a single ETA covers the UK and all three Crown Dependencies.
Validity: 2 years or until your passport expires.

Before you fly: New Zealanders are visa-exempt, but since 1 January 2025 every visa-exempt traveller must hold an approved ETA-IL before boarding. Without it, entry is refused.
Apply: Apply at least 72 hours before arrival on the official government website.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Israel and may charge an additional fee.
Validity: Approval lasts 2 years or until your passport expires.
Stay: For longer than 90 days you must apply to the Population and Immigration Authority.

Area: Schengen short-stay rules.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The Entry/Exit System is fully operational, so expect fingerprints and a facial image at the border instead of a passport stamp.
Bilateral agreement: Italy holds a 1.3.1961 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 3 months. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (all passports). No government guidance explains how to use it at the border, so do not rely on it without checking first.

Visa: New Zealanders are visa-exempt, but the 90 days is a rolling annual allowance rather than per entry.
Passport: Must be valid at least six months beyond your departure from Kiribati.
Source: The controlling legal order is published only as a scanned image, so this rests on the government tourism office's statement.

Visa: New Zealand is on Kuwait's official list of nationalities that may get a visa at the border or online.
Not confirmed: The interior ministry's own portal could not be reached, so the current fee, validity and permitted stay could not be confirmed. Check the portal before you fly. There are also unconfirmed reports the platform is being rebuilt.

Official site: Apply only at laoevisa.gov.la, the official website.
Scam warning: Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Laos and may charge an additional fee.
Entry: Single entry, and it is accepted at 9 designated ports only. Arriving anywhere else means applying for a visa on arrival instead and forfeiting what you paid.
Validity: The approval letter is valid 60 days.

Visa: Libya's official e-visa portal is live and takes individual, agency and company applications, but it is new and unstable.
Sources: Be careful what you read elsewhere. Every Libyan embassy on Libya's own official mission register still publishes nothing about visas. The site most often cited for Libyan visa fees is not on that register at all and contradicts itself, so it is not used here.
In practice: Entry runs through an in-country sponsor or tour operator, tourist visas are not reliably issued, and you should not book on the assumption of getting one.

Area: Liechtenstein is in Schengen through its union with Switzerland but not in the EU.
Visa: It publishes its own entry ordinance, which adopts the EU visa list, so New Zealanders are visa-free.
Long stays: Swiss missions take its long-stay visa applications abroad.
Getting there: There is no airport, so you actually arrive via Switzerland or Austria.
Bilateral agreement: Liechtenstein holds a 1.8.1948 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days. The European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (all passports). No government guidance explains how to use it at the border, so do not rely on it without checking first.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: Luxembourg also holds a bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand dating to 1951. The European Commission lists it at 90 days, but Luxembourg publishes no guidance on how to use it, so do not rely on it at the border.
ETIAS: Not yet in operation; no start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: The Entry/Exit System is live.

Visa: Malaysia's Immigration Department lists New Zealand among countries needing no visa for any purpose of entry, but publishes no permitted stay anywhere on that page.
Arrival card: Complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before you fly. It is an online pre-arrival form that can be filled in up to three days before arrival, and the Canadian and Dutch governments both say it is needed.

Visa: free 30-day visa on arrival, for all nationalities.
Declaration: submit the IMUGA Traveller Declaration online within 96 hours before arrival, and again before departure. Both are compulsory.
Bring: a confirmed onward ticket, a prepaid booking at a registered property or sufficient funds, and a passport valid at least a month.

Schengen: Martinique is a French overseas department and is not in the Schengen area. A Schengen visa gives no right of entry here, and days spent here do not count against your Schengen 90/180.
Visa: New Zealand appears in the French government's exemption table for these territories, with no special conditions attached.

Visa: not required. New Zealand is named in the immigration office's own country table.
Stay: no permitted stay is published for visa-free nationals anywhere.
Entry conditions: a return ticket, adequate funds and confirmed accommodation.
Digital form: the All-in-One Travel Digital Form is a legal requirement, not optional. Refusal or false information can mean a fine of up to MUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years.

Visa: Monaco keeps no exemption list of its own. You need a Schengen visa unless your nationality is exempt, and New Zealand is.
Schengen days: you enter through France and there is no Monegasque border check, so treat your days in Monaco as counting against the Schengen allowance.
Long stay: stays over 90 days need a Monaco national visa via the French consulate.

Visa: New Zealand is on the visa-exempt list on Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular portal, listed as "Nouvelle Zélande" on its Liste des pays dont les ressortissants sont dispensés du visa d'entrée au Maroc.
Conditions: New Zealand carries no annotation on that list. That means no AEVM travel authorisation and no shortened stay, both of which the list flags where they apply (Mali, Congo-Brazzaville and Guinea need an AEVM; Hong Kong and the Maldives are capped at 30 days).
Stay: the list states no duration for New Zealand. 3 months is the threshold in Moroccan law 02-03, beyond which any foreigner must obtain a carte d'immatriculation.
Check: confirm your own case at acces-maroc.ma before flying.

Entry: single entry only. Re-entry needs a fresh visa.
Timing: the approval letter must be used within 90 days of issue, and the 28 days runs from arrival.
Apply: through the official website of the Government of Myanmar.
Scam warning: other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Myanmar and may charge an additional fee.

Visa: get the visitor visa before you travel. Nauru has confirmed that Australians and New Zealanders need one.
Apply: on Form 7 to the Immigration Division of the Department of Justice and Border Control, in person through a representative or online.
On arrival: immigration officers keep your passport and return it later that day or the next morning. This surprises people.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: the Netherlands holds a 1.4.1949 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days. It is still legally in force, and the European Commission lists it as an extension-of-stay agreement (all passports).
Using it: the Dutch government publishes no guidance on how a traveller actually uses it at the border. Do not count on extra days, and do not rely on it without checking first.
ETIAS: not yet in operation. No start date announced.

Visa: required. This is a reversal, so do not rely on any older visa-free answer.
Decree: Disposición No. 002-2026 of Nicaragua's Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería, signed in Managua on 13 February 2026 and in force from 16 February 2026, lists New Zealand at number 86 among the nationalities that "requieren de Visa Consultada, Categoría Migratoria C, para entrar a Nicaragua".
Visa-free list: New Zealand is not on the decree's visa-free list, which runs to 69 countries. Number 50 is Norway, and New Zealand is absent.
Visa Consultada: the most restrictive category. The consulate must refer the application to Managua for authorisation before issuing, so allow substantial lead time.
Fee and stay: the decree sets no fee and no permitted stay.
Apply: through a Nicaraguan consulate well before you travel.

Entry: New Zealanders enter under the free-association provisions of Niue's Immigration Act, which confirms the right of New Zealand citizens to travel to and remain in Niue. They do not enter under the visa-waiver schedule, which grants 30 days and does not list New Zealand.
Conditions: regardless of nationality, Niue requires pre-booked confirmed accommodation for the whole stay, a return or onward ticket, and a passport valid 3+ months. These are refusal-of-entry conditions, not suggestions.

Visa: Norfolk Island applies Australian immigration law, so a New Zealander is granted the Special Category visa (subclass 444) on arrival, exactly as for mainland Australia.
Border: flights use international terminals and you clear Border Force and Biosecurity either way. Biosecurity is strict on food, plant material including wooden articles, and animal products.
Via Sydney: you are cleared into Australia there, not on Norfolk.

Portal: no traveller-facing official portal exists for this destination, and there is unlikely ever to be one. No reachable DPRK immigration or visa site exists. The state news site carries no entry information, and the foreign ministry and tourism domains return nothing.
Tours: all tourism runs through state-approved tour operators. No official source confirms whether tourism is currently open to Western visitors.
Good to know: anything claiming a specific DPRK visa rule has almost certainly come from a tour operator, not the government.

Visa: not needed. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own inbound checker, Do you need a visa?, returns "Visa for foreign citizens: not needed" for New Zealand.
Stay: the ministry publishes no permitted stay alongside that answer and no visa-free country list in text form, so the length of stay is not confirmed here.
Extra route: a separate temporary decision, valid 1 January to 31 December 2026, lets holders of a valid multiple-entry British, American or Canadian visa enter for up to 15 days. That is an additional route, not a limit on the exemption above.

Visa: the Northern Marianas count as the United States for Visa Waiver Program purposes, so a New Zealander travels on an approved ESTA and is admitted for up to 90 days.
Guam-CNMI waiver: a separate waiver gives only 45 days for those islands alone.
Before you fly: an approved ESTA is needed before boarding, and an e-passport is mandatory.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: Norway has held a bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand since 1950, but it publishes no traveller guidance on it. It operates only as an internal instruction telling police not to refuse entry on the ground that you have already spent time in other Schengen states. Do not plan extra days on it.
ETIAS: not yet in operation. No start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: live.

Stay: only 14 days, and it cannot be extended or converted. That is a shorter allowance than most people expect from a Gulf state.
Conditions: a passport valid 6+ months, a return ticket, a confirmed hotel booking, health insurance and sufficient funds. These are stated conditions of the exemption.
Longer stays: buy an e-visa from the Royal Oman Police before you travel.

Visa: there is no Palestinian tourist visa, and Palestine's own embassy says so. Entry to the West Bank runs through Israeli-controlled crossings, and the permission that governs admission is Israel's.
ETA-IL: what you actually need is Israel's ETA-IL, mandatory for visa-exempt travellers since 1 January 2025. Apply at least 72 hours before arrival. It is valid 2 years or until your passport expires.
Gaza: no traveller-accessible route.

Stay: two numbers apply, and both matter. Peru's law sets 183 days accumulated in any 365-day period, not per visit, so multiple trips draw down the same allowance. But Peru's own consular table shows 90 days for New Zealand tourists, and the officer at the border sets what you actually get. Plan on 90.
Work: tourist status does not permit any paid work.

Short stay: a short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival, via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form, for stays of up to 14 days on the same vessel. No fee for short visits.
Longer stay: 15 days–6 months needs advance Entry Clearance, applied for to admin@pitcairn.gov.pn at least 3 months ahead, with a medical exam, chest X-ray and police certificates.
Fee: NZ$150 (non-refundable) for the Long-Term Visitor Visa.
Insurance: mandatory travel/medical insurance with at least US$500,000 medevac cover for all visitors.

Area: Schengen.
Passport: must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid at least 3 months beyond your intended departure. Poland states both conditions explicitly.
ETIAS: not yet in operation. No start date announced.
Entry/Exit System: live, so expect fingerprints and a facial image instead of a stamp.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: Portugal holds a 1.1.1988 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days, listed by the European Commission as an extension-of-stay agreement (ordinary passports). It may allow a further 90 days.
Using it: Portugal publishes no guidance on how to use it. There is nothing on when the clock starts or what to show at the border, and nothing on the MNE visa portal, AIMA, the diplomatic portal or the embassy accredited to New Zealand. Confirm with a Portuguese consulate before relying on it.
ETIAS: not yet in operation. No start date announced.

Visa: Puerto Rico is United States territory for immigration purposes, so the Visa Waiver Program applies and you need an approved ESTA before boarding. An e-passport is mandatory.
ESTA: approval normally lasts 2 years or until your passport expires.
Fee: adjusted for inflation each US financial year, so re-check it after 1 October.

Visa: New Zealand is not on the list of countries eligible for Russia's unified electronic visa. That is worth knowing, because the e-visa is what most travellers assume applies.
Apply: New Zealanders need a conventional visa arranged in advance from the Russian Embassy in Wellington, which requires a visa support letter or invitation.
Changes: the visa type and entry and exit dates cannot be changed or extended once issued.

Visa: New Zealand is not on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries that require visas upon entry into Saint Kitts and Nevis, so no visa is needed.
eTA: an Electronic Travel Authorisation is needed. Since 26 May 2025 the government requires that "every visitor must present an approved eTA before departing their country of origin and on arrival". Only nationals and residents of Saint Kitts and Nevis, the OECS and CARICOM are exempt from the charge.
Apply: through knatravelform.kn or the Saint Kitts and Nevis e-Border app. App applicants get the fast-track biometric corridor on arrival.
Good to know: anything still describing this destination as simply visa-free is out of date.

Visa: New Zealand is on Saint Lucia's list of nationalities not requiring a visa.
Stay: six weeks is shorter than the three or six months most Caribbean states give, so check the date you are stamped to.
Form: all travellers should complete the online immigration and customs form before arrival.
Cruise: one-day cruise passengers are exempt from visas.

Area: the French northern half of the island is an overseas collectivity outside the Schengen area.
Visa: New Zealand appears in the French government's exemption table for Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin, with no conditions.
Sint Maarten: the Dutch southern half of the same island is a separate jurisdiction with its own rules. Nothing here applies to it.

Stay: do not assume 90 days. Singapore publishes no fixed visa-free period and the officer grants what they grant. The High Commission in Wellington says 14 to 30 days is normal, and the extension rules imply a 30-day norm.
Arrival card: the SG Arrival Card is compulsory, free, and must be submitted within 3 days before arrival. Sites charging for it are not official.

Which island: this is the Dutch half of the island and a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, not French Saint Martin.
Bring: a passport issued within the last 10 years, proof of onward or return travel, funds of roughly USD 150–200 a day if you stay in a hotel and medical insurance covering at least USD 15,000 including repatriation.
Entry form: every traveller must also complete the official online Sint Maarten entry form (the ED card) before arrival.

Visa: Somalia moved to a mandatory electronic travel authorisation from 1 September 2025. Embassies no longer process visas in person, and applications go through the portal only.
Not published: no fee, stay or nationality list is published in readable form.
Somaliland: runs its own separate immigration regime, with visa on arrival only at Hargeisa and Berbera airports.
Data breach: Somalia's e-visa platform previously suffered a data breach affecting travellers' personal information (Nov 2025).

Passport: must have at least two unused pages for stamps and be valid at least 30 days beyond your intended departure. Both cause real refusals.
Authorisation: South Africa's new travel authorisation is for visa-required nationalities only, so New Zealanders do not need one.
Traveller declaration: new from 1 July 2026, everyone entering or leaving must submit an online traveller declaration at least 24 hours before departure. It is a customs form, not an entry permit, and it is free.

entries.destination: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

fields.note:
Money: no banks, ATMs or retail economy on the island. The Falkland Islands pound (at par with GBP) is the local currency in name only.
Permit: Entry Control Ordinance 2022 requires a visitor permit for essentially everyone, applied for via eta.entry.gov.gs. Commercial cruise operators typically submit group bookings on passengers' behalf.
Validity: a visitor permit is valid for 40 days (gov.gs).
Late fee: the £50 late fee applies if you apply 8 days or less before arrival.

Visa: visa-free entry for 90 days is permanent under the Korea–New Zealand agreement.
K-ETA: visa-free travellers normally need one, but it has been waived for New Zealand since April 2023. That exemption runs only to 31 December 2026 and has already been extended three times. Re-check before booking anything into 2027. If it lapses, you need a K-ETA before boarding.
Voluntary K-ETA: you may apply for one meanwhile, but the only benefit is skipping the arrival card and the fee is non-refundable.

Area: Schengen.
Bilateral agreement: unlike Germany, Italy, France and a dozen others, Spain holds no bilateral agreement with New Zealand, so there are no extra days here.
Passport: must be valid 3 months beyond departure from the Schengen area and issued within the previous 10 years.
ETIAS: not in operation yet.
Entry/Exit System: live, so you can no longer track your 90/180 from passport stamps.

ETA: New Zealand is one of 40 nationalities getting the tourist ETA free from 25 May 2026. The authorisation is still mandatory. Only the fee is waived.
Apply: before you travel, on the immigration department's own portal.
Second entry: uses the balance of the same 30 days, not a fresh 30.

Portal: no traveller-facing official portal exists for this destination. Sudan is in armed conflict and no functioning national immigration site could be reached.
Permit: Sudan's own embassies say a sponsor must first obtain an entry permit number from the Aliens Department in Khartoum before any visa can be issued. Fees differ by mission.
Good to know: treat this as apply-through-an-embassy-if-at-all.

Visa: Suriname abolished the visa for most nationalities in 2022 and replaced it with a compulsory Entry Fee. You buy the voucher online before departure and show it at check-in. Calling it visa-free would mislead you into boarding without it.
Visa-required list: New Zealand is not on the 21-country visa-required list.
Tourist card: there is no tourist card for New Zealanders.

Visa: the Governor of Svalbard states that foreigners need no visa, work permit or residence permit from the Norwegian authorities in order to travel there. The Norwegian Directorate of Immigration confirms "you do not need a separate residence permit or visa to be allowed to stay on Svalbard".
Stay: there is no maximum stay set by immigration rules.
Schengen: Svalbard is outside the Schengen area but essentially every route there transits mainland Norway, which is inside it. So your days in mainland Norway count against the Schengen 90/180 allowance even though your days on Svalbard do not.
Support: everyone must be able to support themselves there. There is no welfare safety net, and the Governor can require you to leave if you cannot.

Area: Schengen, plus one of only three bilateral agreements with usable published rules.
ETIAS: not in operation yet.
Entry/Exit System: live.
Bilateral agreement: Sweden holds a 1.7.1948 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 3 months, listed by the European Commission as an extension-of-stay agreement (ordinary passports).
Guidance: Sweden does publish traveller guidance, with a worked example. 90 days visa-free in France then a further 90 in Sweden is fine.
Counting rule: time already spent in Sweden or any other Nordic country in the previous six months is deducted. Time in non-Nordic Schengen states is not.
Border: Sweden publishes nothing on border procedure or the Entry/Exit System.

Area: Schengen (via the bilateral arrangements with the EU, not EU membership).
ETIAS: not in operation yet.
Entry/Exit System: live.
Bilateral agreement: Switzerland holds a 1.8.1948 bilateral visa waiver agreement with New Zealand allowing 90 days, listed by the European Commission as an extension-of-stay agreement (all passports).
Conditions: strict. Switzerland states them outright. Stay in Switzerland only for the extra period, carry credible evidence of your time there (accommodation receipts, transport tickets, ATM slips), and leave the whole Schengen Area directly from a Swiss external border. Flying onward to another Schengen country afterwards is expressly not permitted.
Caveat: this is embassy guidance and is not mirrored in the migration secretariat's own instructions to border guards.

Visa: required.
Official site: Syria's foreign ministry site loads but offers consular services for Syrian nationals only, and its eVisa site was not working when checked on 16 Oct 2026.
Rules: the ministry says entry rules are set by Decision No. 128 of 1 July 2025, which it has not published online.
Before you fly: contact a Syrian embassy before you travel.

Visa: visa-exempt for 90 days, counted from the day after arrival. It cannot be extended for New Zealanders. Only Canadian and British passport holders can extend.
Passport: must have 6 months validity.
Bring: a confirmed onward ticket.
Arrival card: the Taiwan Arrival Card has been compulsory since 1 October 2025 and is free. Without it you cannot clear immigration.

Visa: visa-free since January 2022 and still current.
Permit: a separate permit is needed for the Gorno-Badakhshan region. That is the Pamir Highway, Khorugh, Darvoz, Vanj, Rushon, Ishkoshim and Murghob.
Fee: the permit costs USD 20 when issued alongside an e-visa. Tajik embassies and consulates issue it, or you can apply online before you arrive.

Visa: Tokelau is a New Zealand territory, so no permit is needed to enter.
Stay: a New Zealand citizen who is not a Tokelauan may not stay past 10 days without a permit.
Getting there: there is no airport. You sail from Apia in Samoa, the boat runs fortnightly and takes 24 to 32 hours each way, so a realistic round trip will usually exceed 10 days and need a permit.

Visa: required. Trinidad and Tobago exempts the Commonwealth but carves out eleven states by name, and New Zealand is one of them, alongside Australia, Fiji, South Africa and Nigeria. So you need a visa despite the Commonwealth tie.
Arrival card: since March 2026 every traveller must complete the free online arrival or departure card, up to 72 hours before travel.

Visa page: there is no traveller-facing visa page. The foreign ministry site (www.diplomatie.gov.tn) loads, but its visa page returns 404.
Other sites: the Ministry of the Interior and its administrative services portal publish only an application form for foreigners already resident, not an entry rule. No gov.tn domain publishes a visa-exempt country list.
Washington embassy: it sits on a .org rather than a gov.tn domain, so it is not treated as authoritative here.
Contact: a Tunisian consulate directly.

Visa: one of the hardest anywhere. You cannot get one without a letter of invitation certified by the State Migration Service, valid only 3 months from certification.
Tourists: those with no personal host must go through a Turkmen travel agency.
Airport: a visa can be collected at Ashgabat airport, but only if you already hold the certified invitation. That is not visa on arrival in any useful sense.

Visa: Tuvalu issues a visitor's permit on arrival.
Fee: New Zealand is not on the schedule of countries exempt from the permit fee, so expect to pay AUD 100. Australia is not on it either, while the UK, Fiji, Kiribati, Tonga and Samoa are.
Stay: visitors are capped at 3 months in any 12.

Status: not fully confirmed, so re-check before travelling.
Martial law: Ukraine is under martial law and entry conditions can change without notice. Regional access is restricted and the occupied territories need a separate permit.
Conflicting sources: Ukraine's own missions contradict each other. The embassy accredited to New Zealand says no visa is needed, while its missions in the US list New Zealand as e-visa eligible. Ukraine's foreign ministry table, the authoritative source, could not be checked.

ETA: required since 8 January 2025. The fee rose from GBP 16 to GBP 20 on 8 April 2026.
Coverage: one ETA covers the UK, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man for 2 years of multiple journeys, or until your passport expires. Technically these are four separate schemes that recognise each other, so if you are visiting more than one, apply to whichever you will spend most time in.
Transit: not needed for airside transit where you do not pass through border control.

Visa: New Zealand is in the Visa Waiver Program, so you need an approved ESTA before boarding and an e-passport with an electronic chip.
ESTA: approval lasts 2 years or until your passport expires.
Stay: Visa Waiver admission cannot be extended and you cannot change status inside the US.
Fee: inflation-adjusted every US financial year, so re-check it after 1 October.

Visa: New Zealand is on Vanuatu's exempted list, though Vanuatu's own wording is that you 'obtain a tourist visa upon arrival'. There is no advance application either way.
Stay: 120 days is the visa's maximum and it cannot be extended. What an officer actually stamps is not published, and 120 days is far more generous than commonly assumed, so check your stamp.

Visa: the foreign ministry's exemption list naming New Zealand is expressly for entry by air. Nothing official covers land or sea arrivals, so do not assume an overland crossing from Colombia or Brazil is visa-free.
Stay: the immigration authority publishes nothing at all for prospective visitors, but the foreign ministry's own migratory-requirements page sets a maximum tourist stay of 90 days.

Area: a French overseas collectivity outside the Schengen area, with its own entry regime.
Visa: New Zealand is named on the territory's own short-stay exemption list, and the exemption covers all passport types.
Good to know: France's central visa portal does not mention Wallis and Futuna on its New Zealand page. It covers only New Caledonia and French Polynesia, so the territory's own prefecture is the source that matters here.

Visa: tourist entry now runs through Yemen's e-visa portal (yemenevisa.org) via a Yemen-accredited travel agency. That means a group of 10 or more, or an agency-requested urgent visa.
Nationality: New Zealand is on the list of nationalities requiring a visa. There is no independent visa on arrival.

Visa: New Zealand is a Category B country. A visa is required but can be bought at the port of entry, or online beforehand.
Stay: Zimbabwe publishes no permitted stay anywhere official, so do not rely on the 30-days-extendable-to-90 figure that circulates.
KAZA UniVisa: USD 50, covers Zimbabwe and Zambia for 30 days and is the better buy if you are crossing at Victoria Falls more than once.

Good to know: Bahrain's published country lists are no use as a guide. They name all 204 countries and mark every one "conditions apply".
Source: the figures below come from Bahrain's own eligibility engine, queried for this nationality.
Visa: applying online buys a longer stay than turning up does. UK passports get the widest on-arrival range of the four, including a 6-month multiple-entry visa issued at the counter.

Visa: visa-exempt.
Fee: $75 Bonaire Visitor Entry Tax (age 13+; $10 for 12 and under), payable online up to 7 days before arrival, or by card at the airport. It is not a visa fee.
Nature Fee: anyone diving, snorkelling, swimming, windsurfing or kitesurfing also pays a STINAPA Nature Fee of about $40 a year.
Passport: must be valid at least 6 months after arrival.

Visa: visa-free, but the Digital Immigration (DI) card is mandatory. It is free and must be completed within 7 days before departure.
Stay: the 90-day allowance is specific to Curaçao (immigrationcur.org). It is not pooled with Aruba, Sint Maarten or the Caribbean Netherlands for visa-exempt visitors.
Good to know: outside the hurricane belt.

Schengen: the Faroe Islands are not in Schengen and not in the EU, despite being part of the Kingdom of Denmark. A Schengen or Danish visa does not cover the Faroes. ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: time here counts toward the same combined 90 days per 180 shared with Schengen and Greenland (nyidanmark.dk).
Transit: you will usually also transit Copenhagen, which is Schengen itself.

Visa: this changed on 15 July 2026. The FCDO now states plainly that British nationals "do not need a visa to enter Gibraltar for up to 90 days".
Stay: the FCDO says the limit "applies in any 180-day period", and that "any time you spend in Gibraltar will count alongside time spent in the Schengen Area towards this limit".
Sources disagree: Gibraltar's own technical notice says it does not apply to British citizens. But that notice is about visa requirements, which British citizens never needed, and the FCDO applies the stay cap regardless.
Arriving by air: you clear Gibraltar immigration and then Schengen entry checks by Spanish officers, including EES.
UK ETA: Gibraltar is not covered by the UK ETA.
Residents: if you live in Gibraltar or hold a Gibraltar ID card, different rules apply. Check with the Gibraltar Borders and Coastguard Agency.

Schengen: Greenland is not in Schengen and not in the EU. A Schengen or Danish visa does not cover Greenland.
Stay: time here counts toward the same combined 90 days per 180 shared with Schengen and the Faroe Islands (nyidanmark.dk).
Flights: Nuuk's international airport opened in Nov 2024, so there are now direct flights rather than the old Kangerlussuaq routing.
Insurance: travel insurance covering evacuation is strongly advised.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid here and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: euro currency. Hurricane season runs June to November.

Visa: one-month visa issued free at the port of entry under General Security's nationality rules.
Overstay: if you overstay by less than one month, you can leave and pay a fine at departure. If you overstay by more than one month, you must contact General Security's bureau of Arabs and foreigners before you are allowed to leave.

Visa: the FCDO states "you can visit Lesotho for up to 90 days without a visa", with a 90-day temporary permit extension available at the Visa Application Centre in Maseru.
Sources: Lesotho publishes no visa-exempt country list and no per-nationality stay length. Its foreign ministry says only that exempt stays "vary from 1 month to 3 months", waived by Commonwealth membership plus bilateral agreements.
Longer stays: anything longer needs a visa. Lesotho's own e-visa page still reads "eVISA Applications System Suspended", with applications by email to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls.

Visa: visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, fee waived.
Bring: a passport valid 6 months beyond departure, a confirmed return or onward ticket, and any visas needed for onward travel.
Not permitted: extensions, change of status and employment.
Kwajalein Atoll: requires separate US Military entry authorization.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid here and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: Mount Pelée is an active volcano. Hurricane season runs June to November.

Visa: visa-free.
Bring: pre-booked accommodation. It is strictly enforced and you will not be allowed to board without it, because the island simply cannot absorb walk-ups.
Flights: Air New Zealand from Auckland is the only air link (twice weekly to end-Oct 2026, then weekly).
Good to know: one of the world's smallest countries and a raised coral atoll with no beaches to speak of, but exceptional diving.

Visa: a short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival, via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form, for stays of up to 14 days on the same vessel.
Longer stays: 15 days–6 months need advance Entry Clearance, applied for to admin@pitcairn.gov.pn at least 3 months ahead, with a medical exam, chest X-ray and police certificates.
Fee: NZ$150 (non-refundable) for the Long-Term Visitor Visa. No fee for short visits.
Insurance: mandatory travel/medical insurance with at least US$500,000 medevac cover for all visitors.
Support: the FCDO says no travel can be guaranteed safe and there is no British Embassy on Pitcairn (support via the local Pitcairn government).
Import restrictions: apply to alcohol without a licence, honey and used beekeeping equipment, and restricted plant/animal products.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid here and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended, the same instrument covering Guadeloupe, French Guiana, Martinique and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: Piton de la Fournaise is one of the world's most active volcanoes.
Sharks: swimming and surfing are banned or heavily restricted on much of the west coast because of shark attacks. Swim only in the protected lagoons.

Visa: visa-free. French overseas collectivity, outside both Schengen and the EU customs area, with its own visa rules.
Getting there: almost all arrivals connect through Sint Maarten (SXM) by small plane or ferry, so check that territory's rules too.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 18 avril 2012 (the same instrument covering Saint-Martin), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Schengen: Saint Barthélemy is not in the Schengen area.

Visa: you need an entry permit to visit St Helena, and you can apply for one when you arrive.
Fee: £20, payable in cash in British pounds, euros, US dollars or South African rand.
Bring: a return ticket or proof of funds to buy one, details of your accommodation, sufficient funds for your visit and medical insurance that covers medical evacuation.

Visa: visa-free.
Good to know: a small French archipelago off Newfoundland, the last remnant of New France. Not in Schengen.
Getting there: access is via Canada (ferry from Fortune, Newfoundland, or flights from Montreal and Halifax), so you must also meet Canada's entry rules, including an eTA.
Seasonal flight: a direct flight from Paris CDG also operates in summer (weekly, roughly late June to early September, run by Air Saint-Pierre with ASL Airlines France). Check current dates before relying on it.

Stay: the FCDO states that ICA "decides who can enter Singapore and how long they can stay", that "the period of stay permitted is at the discretion of the immigration officer", and that it "is normally between 30 and 90 days for British citizens".
Good to know: Singapore publishes no fixed visa-free period at all, so check the visit pass you are actually given.
Overstay: penalties include fines, imprisonment, caning and deportation.
Arrival card: the SG Arrival Card is compulsory and free within the 3 days before arrival.

Visa: visa-free, but the ED card at entry.sx is mandatory for everyone, including passengers merely transiting to Anguilla, Saba, St Barths or St Kitts.
Fee: the official ED card is free. Other websites that offer to fill it in for you are not operated by the Government of Sint Maarten and may charge a fee.
Good to know: the airport (SXM) also serves French Saint-Martin.

Visa: eTA mandatory for all foreign passports since 1 Sep 2025. Apply via the Immigration & Citizenship Agency before travel.
Somaliland: a separate regime with its own immigration authority and e-visa. The federal authorisation may not be recognised there.
Data breach: Somalia's e-visa platform previously suffered a data breach affecting travellers' personal information (Nov 2025).

Visa: not plain visa-free. British travellers must buy Suriname's Entry Fee voucher online through VFS Global before departure and show it at check-in. Airlines have checked it since 15 January 2024. Apply at least 72 hours ahead.
Fee: single-entry by default. A multiple-entry voucher covering 5 entries in 3 months is sold separately. Children under 3 are exempt from the fee.
Passport: needs 6 months validity and 1 blank page.

Visa: unique. It is a visa-free zone for every nationality on earth under the Svalbard Treaty, and outside Schengen.
Getting there: the catch is that flights route through mainland Norway, which is Schengen, so you must satisfy Norwegian entry rules both ways.
Support: you must be able to support yourself. The Governor can require you to leave otherwise.
Bring: polar bear protection (a firearm and guide) is required outside settlements.

Visa: confirmed visa-free.
Sources: the Airports Authority list grants entry to Commonwealth citizens apart from eleven named exceptions: Fiji, South Africa, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, New Zealand, Tanzania, Australia, Nigeria, Uganda, Cameroon and Papua New Guinea. The UK is not among them. The Ministry of Homeland Security's own country list names the United Kingdom outright.

Visa: visa-free.
Getting there: the only air access is a limited service from Nouméa (New Caledonia) and occasionally Fiji, so your itinerary depends on those territories' rules too.
Good to know: genuinely remote, one of the least-visited places on earth. Not in Schengen. Very limited medical facilities, so evacuation insurance is strongly advised.

Visa: rules mirror Morocco's, but the FCDO publishes a dedicated Western Sahara page (not routed via Morocco).
Border: a passport stamp on arrival is essential. Organised tour groups are generally permitted, but independent travellers could be turned back at the border.

Visa: tourist entry now runs through Yemen's e-visa portal (yemenevisa.org) via a Yemen-accredited travel agency, for a group of 10 or more or an agency-requested urgent visa. There is no independent visa on arrival.
Register: register your passport if staying more than 14 days.

Good to know: Bahrain's published country lists are no guide. They name all 204 countries and mark every one "conditions apply".
Source: the figures below come from Bahrain's own eligibility engine, queried for this nationality.
Stay: applying online buys a longer stay than turning up does.
Visa: US passports are offered a 10 Year multiple-entry visa that other nationalities are not.

Visa: visa-exempt.
Bonaire Visitor Entry Tax: $75 (age 13+; $10 for 12 and under), payable online up to 7 days before arrival, or by card at the airport. It is not a visa fee.
Nature Fee: anyone diving, snorkelling, swimming, windsurfing or kitesurfing also pays a ~$40/yr STINAPA Nature Fee.
Stay: US citizens get the longer 180 days per 365 days, confirmed on Rijksdienst Caribisch Nederland's own tourist-stay page (rijksdienstcn.com). Other nationalities get 90 days per 180.

Change: on 15 July 2026 Gibraltar began running the Schengen short-stay policy, and older '3 months' advice is out of date.
Stay: 90 days in any 180 days. Gibraltar's technical notice says it has aligned "for stays of 90 days in any 180 days", and the USA is named on the visa-exempt list appended to it.
Shared allowance: days in Gibraltar draw down the same 90/180 allowance as Spain and the rest of Schengen, so a Spain-then-Gibraltar trip does not reset anything.
Arriving by air: you clear two sets of checks, Gibraltar immigration, then Schengen entry checks by Spanish officers including EES registration. After that the land border into Spain has no routine immigration checks.
UK ETA: not valid for Gibraltar.

Schengen: not in Schengen and not in the EU. A Schengen or Danish visa does not cover Greenland.
Stay: time here counts toward the same combined 90 days per 180 shared with Schengen and the Faroe Islands (nyidanmark.dk).
Good to know: Nuuk international airport opened Nov 2024, with seasonal direct service from the US east coast.
Insurance: cover for medical evacuation is strongly advised.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: hurricane season is June to November.

Visa: the State Department states that "visas are not required for U.S. citizens visiting for 180 days or fewer".
Stay: Americans are usually granted 30 days at the border. To extend towards the 180-day ceiling, apply to the Office of Immigration at the Ministry of Home Affairs. Plan around 30 days. The 180 is a ceiling you have to go and ask for.
Warning: the State Department also warns that "Lesotho government websites are often outdated".
Source gap: Lesotho publishes no visa-exempt country list and no per-nationality stay length. Its foreign ministry says only that exempt stays "vary from 1 month to 3 months", waived by Commonwealth membership plus bilateral agreements.
Longer stays: anything longer needs a visa. Lesotho's own e-visa page still reads "eVISA Applications System Suspended", with applications by email to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: Mount Pelée is an active volcano. Hurricane season is June to November.

Entry: through Israeli-controlled crossings. There is no Palestinian port of entry, so Israel's rules decide whether you get in.
Gaza: not enterable by ordinary travellers.
Good to know: carry your passport at checkpoints and expect long, unpredictable delays.

Visa: a short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival, via a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form, for stays of up to 14 days on the same vessel.
Longer stays: 15 days-6 months need advance Entry Clearance, applied for to admin@pitcairn.gov.pn at least 3 months ahead, with a medical exam, chest X-ray and police certificates.
Fee: NZ$150 (non-refundable) for the Long-Term Visitor Visa. No fee for short visits.
Insurance: mandatory travel/medical insurance with at least US$500,000 medevac cover for all visitors.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: entry is governed by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended, the same instrument covering Guadeloupe, French Guiana, Martinique and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon), which sets its own 90-day-per-180-day allowance separate from the Schengen 90/180 count.
Good to know: Piton de la Fournaise is highly active.
Sea safety: swimming and surfing are banned or restricted on much of the west coast because of shark attacks. Stick to the protected lagoons.

Visa: not visa-free in practice. Since 26 May 2025 "every visitor must present an approved eTA before departing their country of origin and on arrival".
Fee: only nationals and residents of Saint Kitts and Nevis, the OECS and CARICOM are exempt from the charge.
Apply: at knatravelform.kn or via the Saint Kitts and Nevis e-Border app. App applicants get the fast-track biometric corridor.

Visa: visa-free.
Good to know: a small French archipelago off Newfoundland. Not in Schengen.
Getting there: access is via Canada (ferry from Fortune, Newfoundland, or flights from Montreal and Halifax), so you must also meet Canada's entry rules.
Summer flight: a seasonal direct flight from Paris CDG also operates in summer (weekly, roughly late June to early September, run by Air Saint-Pierre with ASL Airlines France). Check current dates before relying on it.

Stay: do not plan around a guaranteed 90 days. The State Department says "no visa is required for 90 days or less", but Singapore itself publishes no fixed visa-free period. ICA grants a visit pass at the checkpoint and its own warning is to "not stay beyond your Visit Pass validity". Check the pass you are actually given.
Arrival card: the SG Arrival Card with health declaration is compulsory and free, submitted within the 3 days before arrival including the arrival day. Sites charging for it are not official.

Visa: visa-free with a generous 180-day allowance, helped by the 1956 Friendship Treaty giving US citizens broadly Dutch-national treatment.
Arrival card: the ED card at entry.sx is still mandatory for everyone, including transit passengers.
Scam warning: the official ED card is free. Other websites that offer to fill it in for you are not operated by the Government of Sint Maarten and may charge a fee.

Visa: eTA mandatory for all foreign passports (AIC A 10/2025, in force since 1 Sep 2025). Apply via the Immigration & Citizenship Agency before travel.
Good to know: the federal eTA does not reliably cover Somaliland.
Data breach: Somalia's e-visa platform previously suffered a data breach affecting travellers' personal information (Nov 2025).

entries.destination: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

fields.note:
Money: no banks, ATMs or retail economy on the island. The Falkland Islands pound (at par with GBP) is the local currency in name only.
Permit: Entry Control Ordinance 2022 requires a visitor permit for essentially everyone, applied for via eta.entry.gov.gs. Commercial cruise operators typically submit group bookings on passengers' behalf.
Validity: a visitor permit is valid for 40 days (gov.gs).
Fee: the £50 late fee applies if you apply 8 days or less before arrival.

Visa: unique. A visa-free zone for every nationality under the Svalbard Treaty, and outside Schengen.
Getting there: flights route through mainland Norway, which is in Schengen, so Norwegian entry rules apply both ways.
Bring: you must be self-supporting. The Governor can require you to leave otherwise.
Good to know: polar bear protection (firearm and guide) is required outside settlements.

Visa: Trinidad and Tobago's own visa-free lists omit the United States, but the US State Department says no visa is required for stays of 90 days or less (23 April 2026). The two sources disagree. Hop follows the US government's position here.
Bring: evidence of onward travel. If in doubt, confirm with the nearest Trinidad and Tobago mission.

Visa: tourist entry now runs through Yemen's e-visa portal (yemenevisa.org) via a Yemen-accredited travel agency. This means a group of 10 or more, or an agency-requested urgent visa. There is no independent visa on arrival.
Registration: register your passport if staying more than 14 days.

Visa: not needed for stays up to 90 days.
Passport: valid at least 3 months beyond departure and issued within the last 10 years.
Extension: only in exceptional cases (serious personal reasons, force majeure or humanitarian grounds), through the border and migration authority. Otherwise a longer stay needs a residence permit.

Visa: visa-exempt.
Bonaire Visitor Entry Tax: $75 (age 13+; $10 for 12 and under), payable online up to 7 days before arrival, or by card at the airport. It is not a visa fee.
Nature Fee: anyone diving, snorkelling, swimming, windsurfing or kitesurfing also pays about $40 a year to STINAPA.
Advisory: Smartraveller carries no dedicated Bonaire advisory page.

Schengen: not in Schengen and not in the EU. A Schengen or Danish visa does not cover Greenland.
Stay: time here counts toward the same combined 90 days per 180 shared with Schengen and the Faroe Islands (nyidanmark.dk).
Getting there: Nuuk international airport opened Nov 2024.
Insurance: cover for medical evacuation strongly advised. Distances are vast and weather closes routes.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: its own allowance of 90 days per 180 days, separate from the Schengen 90/180 count, set by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended).
Weather: hurricane season June to November.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: its own allowance of 90 days per 180 days, separate from the Schengen 90/180 count, set by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended).
Good to know: Mount Pelée is an active volcano. Hurricane season June to November.

Short visits: a short-term visitor visa is granted on arrival, through a combined immigration and biosecurity declaration form, for stays of up to 14 days on the same vessel. No fee.
Longer stays (15 days–6 months): need advance Entry Clearance. Apply to admin@pitcairn.gov.pn at least 3 months ahead, with a medical exam, chest X-ray and police certificates. NZ$150 (non-refundable) for the Long-Term Visitor Visa.
Insurance: mandatory travel/medical insurance with at least US$500,000 medevac cover for all visitors.

Visa: visa-free.
Schengen: part of the EU but not in Schengen. A Schengen visa is not valid and ETIAS will not apply.
Stay: its own allowance of 90 days per 180 days, separate from the Schengen 90/180 count, set by the arrêté du 26 juillet 2011 (as amended, the same instrument covering Guadeloupe, French Guiana, Martinique and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon).
Volcano: Piton de la Fournaise is highly active.
Sharks: swimming and surfing are banned or restricted on much of the west coast because of shark attacks. Stick to the protected lagoons.

Visa: visa-free. Not in Schengen.
Where: a small French archipelago off Newfoundland.
Getting there: access is via Canada (ferry from Fortune, Newfoundland, or flights from Montreal and Halifax), so you must also meet Canada's entry rules, including an eTA.
Summer flight: a seasonal direct flight from Paris CDG also operates in summer (weekly, roughly late June to early September, run by Air Saint-Pierre with ASL Airlines France). Check current dates before relying on it.

Stay: do not plan around a guaranteed 90 days. Smartraveller says Australians "do not require a visa for stays up to 90 days", but Singapore itself publishes no fixed visa-free period. ICA grants a visit pass at the checkpoint and warns you to "not stay beyond your Visit Pass validity". Check the pass you are actually given.
SG Arrival Card: compulsory and free, with a health declaration. Submit it within the 3 days before arrival, including the arrival day. Sites charging for it are not official.

Visa: visa-free.
ED card: mandatory for everyone at entry.sx, including passengers transiting to Anguilla, Saba, St Barths or St Kitts.
Scam warning: the official ED card is free. Other websites that offer to fill it in for you are not operated by the Government of Sint Maarten and may charge a fee.
Good to know: the airport (SXM) also serves French Saint-Martin.

eTA: mandatory for all foreign passports since 1 Sep 2025. Apply through the Immigration & Citizenship Agency before travel.
Somaliland: a separate regime with its own immigration authority and e-visa. The federal authorisation may not be recognised there.
Data breach: Somalia's e-visa platform previously suffered a data breach affecting travellers' personal information (Nov 2025).

entries.destination: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

fields.note:
Visitor permit: required for essentially everyone under the Entry Control Ordinance 2022. Apply at eta.entry.gov.gs. Commercial cruise operators typically submit group bookings on passengers' behalf.
Validity: a visitor permit is valid for 40 days (gov.gs).
Late fee: £50 if you apply 8 days or less before arrival.
Money: no banks, ATMs or retail economy on the island. The Falkland Islands pound (at par with GBP) is the local currency in name only.

Visa: not granted automatically. Processing can take up to 10 working days if all documents are complete. Sudanese missions list business, official, work, humanitarian and tourist visas.
After arrival: register with the Aliens' Registration Office within 3 days.
Travel permit: internal travel needs a separate permit.

Visa: a visa-free zone for every nationality under the Svalbard Treaty, and outside Schengen.
Getting there: flights route through mainland Norway, which is in Schengen, so Norwegian entry rules apply both ways.
Conditions: you must be self-supporting. The Governor can require you to leave otherwise.
Safety: polar bear protection (firearm and guide) required outside settlements.

Visa: Australia is excluded by name from Trinidad and Tobago's Commonwealth exemption. The Airports Authority list admits Commonwealth citizens but names eleven exceptions: Fiji, South Africa, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, New Zealand, Tanzania, Australia, Nigeria, Uganda, Cameroon and Papua New Guinea. Australia does not appear on the Ministry of Homeland Security's visa-free country list either.
Common mistake: assuming Commonwealth citizens are exempt gets this wrong.

Visa: visa-free for tourism and transit on an ordinary Australian passport. Older e-visa information is out of date: there is no e-visa to buy and no fee to pay.
Stay: Türkiye's foreign ministry words it as 90 days within any 180-day period.
Official passports: holders still need a visa, which is the reverse of the usual pattern.
Passport: allow six months' validity. The requirement is quoted variously as 150 days or six months beyond arrival.

Visa: tourist entry runs through Yemen's e-visa portal (yemenevisa.org) via a Yemen-accredited travel agency: a group of 10 or more, or an agency-requested urgent visa. There is no independent visa on arrival.
Registration: register your passport if staying more than 14 days.
Advisory: all governments advise against all travel to Yemen.

fields.blurb: A new decree, Disposición No. 002-2026, took effect on 16 February 2026 and reshuffled which nationalities need a visa, so treat older answers as unreliable. Nicaragua is also in the CA-4 zone: the 90-day allowance is shared with Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador and does not reset at those borders.

Passports need three blank pages and six months' validity. Child travel rules are unusually strict: carry the original or a certified copy of the full birth certificate for any child aged 17 or under, plus parental consent or documents showing authority to travel when a child travels with one parent, a guardian, another adult or alone.

A free visitor permit is issued at the border: less than 31 days for most nationalities, three months for New Zealand and Australian citizens, so New Zealand sources do not read across. You need proof of onward travel and sufficient funds, and work or study is not allowed. Extensions are applied for locally and carry a fee.

Since 1 October 2026 every foreign visitor needs Tanzania's inbound travel insurance, USD 44 for up to 92 days: from NIC (inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz) if entering through the Mainland, or ZIC (inbound.visitzanzibar.go.tz) through Zanzibar. Fill in the online Traveller's Health Surveillance Form at afyamsafiri.moh.go.tz before you travel or on arrival, and keep the QR code or reference number. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk. Applying online takes about ten days.

A yellow fever certificate is mandatory. Senegal abolished tourist visas for many nationalities in 2015 but not all of them, and there is no official Senegalese e-visa portal. Some passports get a visa on arrival at Dakar Blaise Diagne airport only. Anyone else who needs a visa applies in person at a Senegalese mission.

A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. Where a visa exemption applies it covers tourism only — business, work or study still need a visa. Passports are expected to have more than six months' validity, and photography is restricted near oil and diamond installations.

Visa applications are made online before travel. The portal also mentions visas issued at the border by immigration services, but that is not something to rely on. A hotel booking is required for a tourist visa. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Burundi's exemptions cover only East African Community and Great Lakes member states plus diplomatic passports, so most visitors need a visa. Apply online before travel at migration.gov.bi; the visa is then issued on arrival, and the foreign ministry publishes the fee-free visa categories. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

All non-Cameroonians need a visa and applications are online only. Approval gives an authorisation with a QR code, and the physical visa is printed at the airport or border post on arrival, so travel with the confirmation. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 1 year and over.

No government source publishes an exempt-nationality list; the visa-exempt list circulating online comes from a commercial site last updated in 2019 that is not the airport authority. Apart from the visa on arrival India's government lists for Indian nationals, visas are lodged at an embassy with an invitation letter or mission order, hotel booking and flight plan, and the fee and permitted stay should be confirmed with the mission. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

The practical route is online pre-enrolment well ahead of travel (the UK government advises at least 10 working days), approval in about 48 working hours although it can take longer, then biometrics at the Visa aeroport desk at Abidjan airport, where the visa is printed and handed over on the spot. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Arrange the visa before travel, through the government e-visa portal or a DRC embassy. Fees vary wildly by mission, from EUR 85 in Brussels to GBP 100 in London and USD 120 in Ottawa for broadly the same one-month visa, so check the mission covering you before paying. Allow at least a week, two on a first trip. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

French Guiana is a French department outside Schengen, and a Schengen visa is not valid here. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 1 year and over. Your passport must be valid three months beyond the day you leave, and officers can ask for an onward ticket, accommodation and funds.

Entry is conditional on holding a visa, with exemptions for a short list of nationalities published only as a scanned image. Apply through the e-visa platform or a Gabonese embassy at least five days before travel, arriving via Libreville. Staying beyond 90 days means applying for a residence card after arrival. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Hard currency must be declared. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. Fees are set by each mission rather than nationally, and the visa only gets you to the border — the officer decides how long you may stay. Visa on arrival is not a tourist route: it is a pre-approved emergency permit at USD 200.

Guinea-Bissau publishes no official traveller portal. Germany's foreign office tells German citizens that a visa can be obtained on arrival at the airport (EUR 80 for 30 days) but not at land borders, and that tourist visas should where possible be applied for in advance at the embassy in Brussels. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 1 year and over.

Mali's embassy in Washington lists visa-free entry for ECOWAS citizens and citizens of Algeria, Cameroon, Andorra, Monaco, Chad, Gambia, Morocco, Mauritania and Tunisia. For UK travellers a visa is required, and the application and payment are fully online via the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs website, which directs applicants to the competent embassy or consulate; the Malian Embassy in Brussels covers the UK. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Niger's foreign ministry states that every foreign national needs a visa in the passport at the border; only airside transit is exempt. Visa on arrival exists only by interior ministry authorisation, and only for travellers leaving a country where Niger has no mission. Fees are set by each mission. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

All non-ECOWAS nationals need a visa, obtained either through the immigration department's own e-visa portal (sl-evisa.gov.sl, around USD 80) or from a Sierra Leone mission abroad. Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Sierra Leone and may charge an additional fee. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller.

South Sudan's foreign ministry tells visitors to obtain a visa from a South Sudanese embassy before travel, and missions are few. It also says some travellers may be able to get one on arrival, which is too conditional to rely on. An official e-visa portal exists but publishes no fee, eligibility list or stay length in readable form. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. Visa validity runs from the day the visa is collected, not from the day you arrive.

Togo no longer issues visas on arrival, so the e-visa must be obtained before you fly. Apply at least seven working days before your flight. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 9 months or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

This is Congo-Brazzaville, not to be confused with the DRC in Kinshasa. The foreign ministry says most travellers need a visa, applied for at the nearest Congolese embassy or consulate, and publishes no exemption list. Expect to need a photo, a letter of invitation and proof of accommodation; the fee and permitted stay are not published. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Visa on arrival was discontinued in May 2025, so entry must be arranged before you fly. All arrivals must also complete the online Landing Card and Health Declaration within 72 hours of departure. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. Nigeria runs two official portals, so check you are on the government one. Other websites that offer to submit the application for you are not operated by the Government of Nigeria and may charge an additional fee.

A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. Liberia's visa on arrival is not a walk-up service — you apply and pay online before flying and the sticker is issued at the airport on landing.

An online visa application form is confirmed working (gov.uk, ~72-hour processing). Expect to need an invitation letter from a local sponsor, a police clearance certificate less than 3 months old and proof of about USD 1,000 per month of stay. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over. An embassy route also remains available.

Apply online through the border police portal before travel; the approval letter is exchanged for the visa on arrival at Conakry. Guinea publishes no list of waiver countries, so a visa is the default assumption. The site visa.ambaguinee.org is a private operator, not the official site. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 9 months and over.

Since 5 January 2025 the e-visa must be held before boarding — it is no longer issued at the border. Biometrics are captured on arrival. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of every arriving traveller aged 1 year and over. Mauritania's foreign ministry publishes its list of visa-waiver agreements; outside North and West Africa they cover only diplomatic, service or official passports.

A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 9 months or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk. Every arriving and departing passenger also pays a USD 20 (or D1000) Securiport airport fee — that is not a visa fee and is collected separately.

Aruba is part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands but sets its own entry rules. Every traveller, children included, must complete the online ED card within 7 days before travel and show it to the airline. Air arrivals pay a USD 20 sustainability fee. Use the official website, edcardaruba.aw. Other websites that offer to fill the ED card in for you are not operated by the Government of Aruba and may charge a fee. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 9 months or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

Bolivia sorts nationalities into three groups, and which group you fall into decides both whether you need a visa and whether a reciprocity fee applies. Visitors who enter without a visa are stamped in for 30 days; two further 30-day extensions can be requested from the migration directorate, capped at 90 days in any year. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from a country with yellow fever risk.

Every traveller, exempt or not, must pre-register on the EASE platform up to 5 days before travel and pay the airport security tax of about EUR 31; paying at the border instead costs more. Where a visa on arrival applies, it is not available at every entry point. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from a country with yellow fever risk.

Every visitor needs a visa. The government e-visa portal is the official route, and approval before you fly avoids depending on what the airport issues on the day. Your passport must be valid six months on arrival, and you need proof of onward travel. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or transit more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk.

Applications go to an Eritrean embassy or consulate, which forwards them to the Immigration Office in Asmara, so allow up to four weeks. The link is the Washington mission's own visa page, not a national portal, so its fees and forms apply there only. Internal travel permits are required to leave Asmara.
